rules.name: Virtual Link as unidirectional logical communication path

constraint.value: A Virtual Link (VL) is a unidirectional logical communication path from one source End System to one or more destination End Systems. It defines a multicast flow of AFDX frames.

rules.source_quote: Virtual Link: A Virtual Link (VL) is a unidirectional logical communication path from one source End System to one or more destination End Systems.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by sending frames from multiple source End Systems on the same VL or by sending bidirectional traffic on a VL.

rules.name: Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAG) definition
rules.source_quote: The Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAG) is the minimum time interval between the start of transmission of two consecutive frames of the same VL. The BAG is configurable and shall be one of the following values: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, or 128 ms.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by sending frames with a BAG not in the allowed list (e.g., 3 ms or 200 ms).

rules.name: Maximum frame size (Lmax) per VL
rules.source_quote: Each VL is characterized by a maximum frame size (Lmax) which shall be between 64 and 1518 bytes.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by sending frames smaller than 64 bytes or larger than 1518 bytes on a VL.

rules.name: Minimum time interval between frames of the same VL

constraint.value: The End System shall ensure that the time interval between the start of transmission of two consecutive frames of the same VL is at least the configured BAG.

rules.source_quote: The End System shall ensure that the time interval between the start of transmission of two consecutive frames of the same VL is at least the configured BAG.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by sending frames of the same VL with a time interval less than the configured BAG.

rules.name: Maximum jitter for frame transmission
rules.source_quote: The maximum jitter introduced by the End System for any VL shall not exceed 500 microseconds.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by introducing jitter greater than 500 μs for frames of a VL.

rules.name: MAC destination address format for AFDX

constraint.value: The MAC destination address shall be a multicast address in the range 01-00-5E-00-00-00 to 01-00-5E-7F-FF-FF.

rules.source_quote: The MAC destination address shall be a multicast address in the range 01-00-5E-00-00-00 to 01-00-5E-7F-FF-FF.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by using a unicast or broadcast MAC destination address, or a multicast address outside the specified range.

rules.name: MAC source address uniqueness

constraint.value: The MAC source address shall be unique for each End System in the AFDX network.

rules.source_quote: The MAC source address shall be unique for each End System in the AFDX network.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by sending frames with a MAC source address that duplicates another End System's address.

rules.name: Redundant frame transmission on separate networks

constraint.value: Each frame shall be transmitted on two independent networks (A and B) to provide redundancy.

rules.source_quote: Redundancy is provided by transmitting each frame on two independent networks (A and B).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by sending frames on only one network or on more than two networks.

rules.name: Sequence number increment per VL

constraint.value: The sending End System shall increment the sequence number for each frame transmitted on a VL, modulo 256.

rules.source_quote: The sending End System shall increment the sequence number for each frame transmitted on a VL, modulo 256.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by sending frames with non-incrementing, repeating, or out-of-order sequence numbers.

rules.name: Sequence number validation at receiving End System

constraint.value: The receiving End System shall validate the sequence number of each received frame to detect frame loss, duplication, or out-of-order delivery.

rules.source_quote: The receiving End System shall validate the sequence number of each received frame to detect frame loss, duplication, or out-of-order delivery.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by sending frames with invalid sequence numbers (e.g., gaps, duplicates, or non-sequential values).

rules.name: Redundancy management at receiving End System

constraint.value: The receiving End System shall use the sequence number to select the first valid frame received (from either network A or B) and discard subsequent duplicates.

rules.source_quote: The receiving End System shall use the sequence number to select the first valid frame received (from either network A or B) and discard subsequent duplicates.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by sending frames with identical sequence numbers but different payloads to test duplicate handling.

rules.name: Sampling service frame transmission interval
rules.source_quote: The Sampling Service shall transmit frames at regular intervals defined by the BAG (Bandwidth Allocation Gap).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames at intervals outside the 1-128 ms range (e.g., 0.5 ms or 200 ms).

rules.name: Sampling service frame size limit
rules.source_quote: The Sampling Service shall not transmit frames larger than the configured Lmax (Maximum Frame Size).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames smaller than 64 bytes or larger than 1471 bytes.

rules.name: Sampling service frame replacement

constraint.value: Newer frames shall replace older frames in the reception buffer if the buffer is full.

rules.source_quote: In reception, the Sampling Service shall replace the oldest frame in the buffer with the newest one if the buffer is full.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames that do not follow the replacement policy (e.g., dropping newer frames).

rules.name: Queuing service frame transmission order

constraint.value: Frames shall be transmitted in the order they are received (FIFO).

rules.source_quote: The Queuing Service shall transmit frames in the order they are received (First-In-First-Out).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames out of order (e.g., reordering or prioritizing later frames).

rules.name: Queuing service frame buffer overflow

constraint.value: If the reception buffer is full, the oldest frame shall be discarded to make room for the newest frame.

rules.source_quote: In reception, if the buffer is full, the Queuing Service shall discard the oldest frame to accommodate the newest one.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames that cause the buffer to drop newer frames instead of older ones.

rules.name: AFDX frame structure without fragmentation

constraint.value: AFDX frames shall not be fragmented and shall include a UDP/IP header followed by the payload.

rules.source_quote: The structure of an AFDX frame without fragmentation shall consist of a UDP/IP header followed by the payload.
rules.source_section: 3.4.1.2 Structure of an AFDX Frame Without Fragmentation
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending fragmented frames or frames with malformed UDP/IP headers.

rules.name: IP source address format

constraint.value: The IP source address shall be a valid IPv4 address assigned to the transmitting End System.

rules.source_quote: The IP source address shall be a valid IPv4 address assigned to the transmitting End System.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by using invalid IPv4 addresses (e.g., 0.0.0.0, multicast addresses, or addresses not assigned to the End System).

rules.name: IP destination address format

constraint.value: The IP destination address shall be a valid IPv4 address assigned to the receiving End System or a multicast group.

rules.source_quote: The IP destination address shall be a valid IPv4 address assigned to the receiving End System or a multicast group.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by using invalid IPv4 destination addresses (e.g., 255.255.255.255, or addresses not assigned to any End System).

rules.name: Frame filtering introduction

constraint.value: Switches shall filter incoming frames based on predefined criteria to ensure only valid frames are forwarded.

rules.source_quote: The filtering function shall ensure that only frames meeting predefined criteria are forwarded through the switch.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames that do not meet filtering criteria (e.g., invalid MAC addresses, incorrect VLAN tags).

rules.name: Traffic policing introduction

constraint.value: Switches shall police incoming traffic to ensure it complies with configured bandwidth and frame size limits.

rules.source_quote: The policing function shall monitor and enforce compliance with configured bandwidth and frame size limits for each Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending traffic that exceeds bandwidth limits (e.g., sending frames faster than the BAG) or exceeds Lmax.

rules.name: AFDX communication port number range
rules.source_quote: AFDX Communication Port numbers shall be allocated in the range 1024 to 65535.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by using port numbers outside the 1024-65535 range (e.g., 0, 1023, or 65536).

rules.name: SAP port number range
rules.source_quote: SAP Port numbers shall be allocated in the range 0 to 1023.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by using SAP port numbers outside the 0-1023 range (e.g., 1024 or 65535).

rules.name: Frame filtering enforcement

constraint.value: AFDX switches must filter incoming frames based on predefined configuration tables to ensure only valid frames are forwarded to their destination Virtual Links (VLs).

rules.source_quote: 4.2.1 Frame Filtering
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with invalid destination MAC addresses or VL IDs not configured in the filtering table to test if the switch drops them.

rules.name: Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAG) enforcement
rules.source_quote: 4.2.2 Traffic Policing
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send frames at intervals shorter than the configured BAG to test if the policing function discards or marks them as non-compliant.

rules.name: Maximum frame size (Lmax) enforcement
rules.source_quote: 4.2.2 Traffic Policing
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames exceeding the configured Lmax for a VL to test if the policing function discards them.

rules.name: Virtual Link (VL) based switching

constraint.value: AFDX switches must forward frames based on their Virtual Link (VL) identifier, not solely on MAC addresses.

rules.source_quote: 4.4 Switching Function
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with valid MAC addresses but invalid or unconfigured VL IDs to test if the switch drops them.

rules.name: AFDX addressing policy enforcement

constraint.value: AFDX switches and end systems must enforce a strict addressing policy where frames are only accepted if their destination MAC address matches the configured VL or multicast group.

rules.source_quote: 4.5.2 Addressing Policy
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with destination MAC addresses that do not match any configured VL or multicast group to test if the switch or end system drops them.

rules.name: Monitoring function enforcement

constraint.value: AFDX switches must monitor network traffic for compliance with configured parameters (e.g., BAG, Lmax) and report violations.

rules.source_quote: 4.6 Monitoring Function
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate non-compliant frames (e.g., exceeding BAG or Lmax) to test if the switch logs or reports violations.

rules.name: Initialization sequence enforcement

constraint.value: AFDX devices must follow a predefined initialization sequence before entering operational mode, including self-tests and configuration validation.

rules.source_quote: 4.8.2.1 Initialization Sequence
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can simulate an AFDX device skipping initialization steps or sending frames before completing initialization to test if the network rejects or ignores them.

rules.name: Operational mode constraints

constraint.value: In OPS (Operational Mode), AFDX devices must only transmit and receive frames that comply with their configured VLs, BAG, and Lmax parameters.

rules.source_quote: 4.8.3 OPS: Operational Mode
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames in OPS mode that violate VL, BAG, or Lmax constraints to test if the device discards or reports them.

rules.name: Passive mode constraints

constraint.value: In PASSIVE mode, AFDX devices must not transmit any frames but must continue to receive and process frames as per their configuration.

rules.source_quote: 4.8.6 PASSIVE
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can attempt to transmit frames from a device in PASSIVE mode to test if the device ignores or rejects them.

rules.name: Quiet mode constraints

constraint.value: In QUIET mode, AFDX devices must not transmit or receive any frames, effectively isolating the device from the network.

rules.source_quote: 4.8.7 QUIET
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can attempt to send frames to or from a device in QUIET mode to test if the device ignores all traffic.

rules.name: AFDX_network_determinism_requirement

constraint.value: AFDX network must exhibit deterministic behavior for flight-critical systems

rules.source_quote: The purpose of this document is to define a deterministic network: Avionics Full Duplex Switched Ethernet (AFDX™).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate non-deterministic traffic patterns (e.g., random bursts, variable timing) to test if the network maintains deterministic behavior.

rules.name: mandatory_protocol_stack_layers

value: Network application layers (Sampling, Queuing, SAP, TFTP, SNMP)

rules.source_quote: The requirements listed in this document aim at specifying interoperable functional elements: • Data link: MAC, VL addressing concept • Network: IP, ICMP • Transport: UDP, TCP (optional) • Network application layers: Sampling, Queuing, SAP, TFTP and SNMP
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with unsupported protocols (e.g., non-UDP transport, non-IP network layer) to test if the network rejects or misroutes them.

rules.name: optional_transport_protocol
rules.source_quote: Transport: UDP, TCP (optional)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate TCP traffic to test if the network handles or rejects it (since TCP is optional).

rules.name: physical_layer_compliance

constraint.value: ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions

rules.source_quote: Physical layer is not specified here, but should be any of the ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions.

rules.name: AFDX_LRU_interoperability

constraint.value: Any AFDX-compliant LRU (including switch) must be connectable to any AFDX network if Form and Fit requirements are respected

rules.source_quote: This means that any AFDX compliant LRU (including switch) can be connected to any AFDX network, as far as the Form and Fit requirements (specific to the System and not specified in this document) are respected.

rules.name: IEEE_802_3_integration

constraint.value: IEEE Standard 802.3, 2000 Edition, is an integral part of this specification and required for implementation

rules.source_quote: IEEE Standard 802.3, 2000 Edition, is considered an integral part of this specification and is considered required reading.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames violating IEEE 802.3 (e.g., invalid MAC addressing, malformed Ethernet frames) to test if the AFDX network enforces compliance.

rules.name: AFDX as a deterministic network subset

constraint.value: AFDX is a deterministic subset of a profiled IEEE 802.3 Ethernet network, ensuring timely delivery and quality of service for safety-critical systems.

rules.source_quote: The AFDX network is a special case of a profiled network. A deterministic network may communicate with a wider profiled network and by inference, with a compliant network through routers or gateways.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate non-deterministic traffic (e.g., bursts violating BAG or jitter constraints) to test if the network enforces determinism.

rules.name: Timely delivery for safety-critical systems

constraint.value: Control and avionics systems require complete, up-to-date data delivered in a timely fashion for real-time communication.

rules.source_quote: Control systems generally, and avionics systems in particular, rely on having complete and up to date data delivered from source to receiver in a timely fashion. For safety critical systems reliable 'real time' communication links are essential.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could introduce delays or out-of-order frames to test if the network detects or mitigates untimely delivery.

rules.name: Specification precedence over IEEE 802.3

constraint.value: In case of conflict between ARINC 664 Part 7 and IEEE 802.3, ARINC 664 Part 7 takes precedence.

rules.source_quote: In case of a conflict between this Specification and the applicable ISO and IEEE standards, this Specification should have precedence.

rules.name: Restriction of IEEE 802.3 options

constraint.value: ARINC 664 Part 7 restricts IEEE 802.3 options to remove ambiguity or address aeronautical environment conflicts.

rules.source_quote: The philosophy of this Specification is to define changes to the provisions of IEEE 802.3 only when the aeronautical environment or user desires conflict with the provisions of IEEE 802.3, or when it is necessary to remove ambiguity by restricting the options available to implementers.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic using unsupported IEEE 802.3 options (e.g., non-standard frame sizes or protocols) to test if the network rejects or ignores them.

rules.name: Total end-to-end latency formula

constraint.value: L = Ts + Tm + Tr

rules.source_quote: the total latency, L, is : L = Ts + Tm + Tr
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject frames with artificially inflated Ts, Tm, or Tr values to violate the expected latency formula and observe if the network enforces or logs latency deviations.

rules.name: Constant end-to-end latency in point-to-point system
rules.source_quote: the time taken to deliver a message, through the network, from the emitter to the receiver is constant
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could introduce variable delays in frame transmission or switching to violate the constant latency rule and observe if the network detects or compensates for the violation.

rules.name: Jitter due to frame contention in switch

constraint.value: Tj = (8 * M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap

rules.source_quote: Tj = (8 x M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap (it is assumed that the frames are of equal size)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames of unequal or oversized lengths to violate the equal size assumption and observe if the switch correctly calculates or enforces jitter limits.

rules.name: First frame latency through switch

constraint.value: La = Ts + Tm1 + Tsw + (8 * M) / Nbw + Tm2 + Tr

rules.source_quote: Latency for the first frame: La = Ts + Tm1 + Tsw + ( 8 x M )/Nbw + Tm2 + Tr
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could manipulate frame size (M) or bandwidth (Nbw) to violate the latency formula and observe if the switch enforces or logs latency deviations.

rules.name: Delayed frame latency through switch

constraint.value: Lb = La + Tj

rules.source_quote: Latency for the delayed frame: Lb = La + Tj
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject frames with artificially high jitter (Tj) to violate the delayed frame latency formula and observe network behavior.

rules.name: Total switch latency definition

constraint.value: Tw = Tsw + output_buffer_latency

rules.source_quote: Tw being the total latency in the switch, in seconds (Tsw + output buffer latency)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate excessive output buffer latency to violate the total switch latency constraint and observe if the switch enforces or logs the violation.

rules.name: No bandwidth limitation in short time periods
rules.source_quote: over any arbitrarily short period of time the bandwidth is unlimited
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic bursts exceeding the nominal bandwidth to test if the network enforces bandwidth limits over short time periods.

rules.name: Independent end-to-end links
rules.source_quote: a fault in one end system will not affect the ability of fault free end systems to communicate
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a fault in one end system and observe if other end systems continue to communicate without disruption.

rules.name: Store-and-forward buffering in switch
rules.source_quote: the store and forward capacity results in the need to buffer complete frames
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject incomplete or fragmented frames to test if the switch enforces store-and-forward buffering rules.

rules.name: Bandwidth Regulation via Bounded Arrival

constraint.value: Frame delivery must follow a bounded arrival distribution to ensure exact bandwidth regulation and limit bandwidth fault effects.

rules.source_quote: In an AFDX network, the analysis also assumes that the transmitting end-systems are not synchronized, but that frame delivery follows a bounded arrival distribution. This bounded arrival implies exact bandwidth regulated traffic control.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with inter-frame gaps violating the bounded arrival distribution (e.g., bursty traffic exceeding the regulated bandwidth).

rules.name: Maximum Bandwidth Allocation for Virtual Link

constraint.value: Lmax / T_GAP

rules.source_quote: The maximum bandwidth allocated to this VL is: Lmax/T GAP.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames exceeding the maximum bandwidth by sending frames larger than Lmax or with inter-frame gaps smaller than T_GAP.

rules.name: Flexible Bandwidth Usage for Virtual Link

constraint.value: A VL may use less bandwidth by increasing the frame interval or reducing frame size at any time.

rules.source_quote: The VL may use less bandwidth through an increased frame interval or smaller frames at any time.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could test network resilience by dynamically varying frame intervals or sizes within a VL, but this is not a violation. Violations would involve exceeding Lmax or T_GAP.

rules.name: Ordinal Integrity within Virtual Link
rules.source_quote: For this reason AFDX requires ordinal integrity of frames within a Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate ordinal integrity by reordering frames within a VL (e.g., sending frame 3 before frame 2).

rules.name: Bounded End-to-End Latency

constraint.value: A firm, mathematically provable upper bound on end-to-end frame transit delay must be guaranteed.

rules.source_quote: A guaranteed service provides a firm, mathematically provable, upper bound on end-to-end frame transit delay.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic patterns that cause latency to exceed the guaranteed upper bound (e.g., by overloading switches or violating BAG).

rules.name: Guaranteed Bandwidth for Virtual Link
rules.source_quote: to guarantee a bounded delay implies to guarantee a certain bandwidth at the link level.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate guaranteed bandwidth by exceeding the allocated bandwidth for a VL (e.g., sending frames too frequently or with excessive size).

rules.name: Bounded Delay Jitter for Flow

constraint.value: A bound to the delay jitter for a flow must be mathematically computable, though not fixed.

rules.source_quote: Particular delay jitter for a flow (end-to-end transit delay variation between any two frames of the same flow) is not fixed since it depends on the global network traffic at a given time. Nevertheless, a bound to the delay jitter can be mathematically computed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic that causes delay jitter to exceed the computed bound (e.g., by introducing variable delays or congestion).

rules.name: Unidirectional Connection

constraint.value: A Virtual Link defines a logical unidirectional connection from one source end-system to one or more destination end-systems.

rules.source_quote: A Virtual Link defines a logical unidirectional connection from one source end-system to one or more destination end-systems, shown in Figure 3-2.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate a VL with bidirectional traffic or multiple source end-systems to violate unidirectionality.

rules.name: Single Source End System

constraint.value: Only one End System within the Avionics network should be the source of any one VL.

rules.source_quote: Only one End System within the Avionics network should be the source of any one VL.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate multiple end-systems transmitting frames for the same VL ID to violate source uniqueness.

rules.name: Dedicated Maximum Bandwidth

constraint.value: Each Virtual Link has a dedicated maximum bandwidth allocated by the System Integrator.

rules.source_quote: Each Virtual Link has a dedicated maximum bandwidth. This bandwidth is allocated by the System Integrator.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic exceeding the allocated bandwidth for a VL to test enforcement.

rules.name: Logical Bandwidth Isolation

constraint.value: The ES should provide logical isolation with respect to available bandwidth among the Virtual Link(s) it supports. Regardless of the attempted utilisation of a VL by one partition, the available Bandwidth on any other VL is unaffected.

rules.source_quote: The ES should provide logical isolation with respect to available bandwidth among the Virtual Link(s) it supports. Regardless of the attempted utilisation of a VL by one partition, the available Bandwidth on any other VL is unaffected.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate excessive traffic on one VL to observe if bandwidth isolation is maintained for other VLs.

rules.name: Ordinal Integrity

constraint.value: For each Virtual Link, the End System should maintain the ordering of data as delivered by a partition, for both transmission and reception.

rules.source_quote: For each Virtual Link, the End System should maintain the ordering of data as delivered by a partition, for both transmission and reception (ordinal integrity).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could reorder frames within a VL to test if ordinal integrity is enforced.

rules.name: Source Partition Exclusivity

constraint.value: One Virtual Link should not be shared by two or more source partitions.

rules.source_quote: One Virtual Link should not be shared by two or more source partitions.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate multiple partitions transmitting on the same VL to test exclusivity.

rules.name: BAG Definition
rules.source_quote: The Traffic shaping function of the ES should be able to handle BAG values in range 1 ms to 128 ms. These values should satisfy the following formula: BAG=2^k [in ms], (k integer in range 0 to 7).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could use BAG values outside the allowed range (e.g., 3 ms, 5 ms) or non-power-of-two values.

rules.name: BAG Enforcement

constraint.value: The frame flow is regulated to guarantee the BAG for each VL. The traffic regulator should shape the flow to send no more than one frame in each interval of BAG milliseconds.

rules.source_quote: To guarantee the BAG for each VL the frame flow is regulated as shown in Figure 3-5. On a per VL basis the traffic regulator (traffic shaping function) should shape the flow to send no more than one frame in each interval of BAG milliseconds.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could transmit multiple frames within a single BAG interval to test BAG enforcement.

rules.name: Jitter Definition

constraint.value: 0 < Jitter < MaxBAG

rules.source_quote: 0 < Jitter < MaxBAG
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could introduce jitter values outside the allowed range (e.g., 0 ms, equal to or exceeding BAG) to test jitter bounds.

rules.name: Maximum Frame Size
rules.source_quote: The End System should accommodate VL frames up to a size of 1518 bytes in both transmission and reception.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames smaller than 64 bytes or larger than 1518 bytes to test frame size enforcement.

rules.name: Maximum Usable Bandwidth

constraint.value: maximum_usable_bandwidth = Lmax / BAG

rules.source_quote: The maximum usable bandwidth of each VL is characterised by its BAG and its authorized Lmax (maximum VL frame size). The maximum usable bandwidth = Lmax / BAG in Kbytes per seconds.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic exceeding the calculated maximum bandwidth (Lmax/BAG) to test bandwidth enforcement.

rules.name: Traffic Shaping Function

constraint.value: The End System should regulate transmitted data on a per VL basis using a Traffic Shaping Function.

rules.source_quote: The End System should regulate transmitted data on a per VL basis, since this Traffic Shaping Function (exact knowledge of flow characteristics) is the basis of the determinism analysis.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could bypass the traffic shaping function to transmit unregulated traffic and observe network behavior.

rules.name: No Transmission Without Data

constraint.value: A frame will not be transmitted while a VL is eligible but has no data for transmission.

rules.source_quote: A frame will not be transmitted while a VL is eligible but has no data for transmission.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a VL transmitting empty or invalid frames when no data is available.

rules.name: BAG value constraints
rules.source_quote: BAG values are limited to powers of 2 in order to simplify the ES design. If a partition needs to transmit data less often than 128 ms, the BAG value 128 will be used.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate traffic with a BAG value not in [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128] ms, e.g., 3 ms or 200 ms.

rules.name: Technological latency upper bound in transmission
rules.source_quote: The technological latency of the end-system in transmission should be bounded and lower than 150 μs + frame delay.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can simulate an end system introducing latency exceeding 150 μs + frame_delay for a transmitted frame.

rules.name: Technological latency upper bound in reception
rules.source_quote: The technological latency of the end-system in reception should be bounded and lower than 150 μs.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can simulate an end system introducing reception latency exceeding 150 μs for a received frame.

rules.name: MAC layer frame processing rate

constraint.value: Process received frames at full frame rate of the medium and appropriate frames are made available to the partition at full frame rate of the medium.

rules.source_quote: Process received frames at full frame rate of the medium and appropriate (selected) frames are made available to the partition at full frame rate of the medium.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a burst of frames exceeding the maximum frame rate (148800 frames/s) to test if the MAC layer drops frames or introduces delays.

rules.name: MAC layer back-to-back frame transmission

constraint.value: Transmit frames back to back.

rules.source_quote: Transmit frames back to back.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can test if the MAC layer introduces gaps between frames when transmitting back-to-back frames.

rules.name: Maximum frame rate per attachment
rules.source_quote: For the shortest frame this corresponds to a maximum frame rate per attachment of: 64 bytes (frame) + 12 bytes (IFG) + 7 bytes (Preamble) + 1 byte (SFD) = 84 bytes to transmit at 100 Mbits/s. Equivalent to a duration of 6.72 μs per frame (about 148800 frames per second).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate traffic exceeding 148800 frames/s to test if the MAC layer can handle the load.

rules.name: Maximum allowed jitter in transmission (formula 1)
rules.source_quote: In transmission, the maximum allowed jitter on each VL at the output of the end-system should comply with both of the following formulas: ... max_jitter ≤ 40 + (8 * Lmax) / (Nbw / 1000000).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate traffic with jitter exceeding the value calculated by the formula for a given Lmax and Nbw.

rules.name: Maximum allowed jitter in transmission (formula 2)
rules.source_quote: In transmission, the maximum allowed jitter on each VL at the output of the end-system should comply with both of the following formulas: ... sum(max_jitter for all VLs) ≤ 500 μs.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate traffic where the cumulative jitter across all VLs exceeds 500 μs.

rules.name: Global jitter upper bound
rules.source_quote: In all cases, the jitter is bounded at 500μs to limit the impact on determinism for the whole network.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate traffic with jitter exceeding 500 μs on a single VL.

rules.name: Maximum Latency for Single Frame Transmission

constraint.value: MAX_Latency_i ≤ BAG_i + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission

rules.source_quote: the total allowed latency for a given VLi is: MAX_Latency i ≤ BAG i + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with transmission delays exceeding BAG_i + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission to violate this constraint.

rules.name: Maximum Latency for Bursty Frame Transmission

constraint.value: MAX_Latencyi (frame_p) ≤ p * BAGi + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission

rules.source_quote: the maximum latency of the frame number p should be bounded according to the following formula: MAX_Latencyi (frame_p) ≤ p * BAGi + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate bursts of frames where the p-th frame exceeds p * BAGi + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission.

rules.name: Bandwidth Limitation per Virtual Link

constraint.value: Transmission of frames on a Virtual Link must be delayed according to the BAG_i to comply with bandwidth limitations.

rules.source_quote: The transmission will be delayed according to the bandwidth limitation of the VL (traffic shaping).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames violating BAG_i by sending them faster than the allowed interval.

rules.name: MAC Destination Address Format

value.constant_field: 32 bits (system integrator-defined, same for all ES in the network)

rules.source_quote: A MAC destination address in the AFDX frame should be a Group and Locally Administered address and should be compliant with the following format. 48 bits: xxxx xx11 xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with MAC destination addresses violating the 'xx11' pattern in the first byte or incorrect Virtual Link Identifier.

rules.name: MAC Source Address Format
rules.source_quote: The Constant field is set to '0000 0010 0000 0000 0000 0000' as shown in Figure 3-11. The least significant bit of the first byte indicates the Individual Address = 0. The second to least significant bit of the first byte indicates the locally administered address = 1.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with MAC source addresses violating the constant field, LSB, or Interface_ID constraints.

rules.name: MAC Source Address Interface_ID Validity
rules.source_quote: Interface_ID Meaning: 001 = Network A, 010 = Network B
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with Interface_ID values outside [1, 2] (e.g., 0, 3-7).

rules.name: Redundant Network Identification via Interface_ID

constraint.value: The Interface_ID indicates to which redundant AFDX network(s) the Ethernet MAC controller is connected (Network A or Network B).

rules.source_quote: The Interface_ID, defined in Figure 3-12, indicates to which redundant AFDX network(s) the Ethernet MAC controller is connected.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with mismatched Interface_ID and actual network path (e.g., Interface_ID=1 on Network B).

rules.name: Redundant Frame Transmission

constraint.value: Each frame must be transmitted on both redundant networks (A and B) by default.

rules.source_quote: In default mode each frame is sent across both of two networks.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by transmitting a frame on only one network or on neither network.

rules.name: First Valid Wins Policy

constraint.value: The first frame received from either network with the next valid sequence number must be accepted; subsequent frames with the same sequence number must be discarded.

rules.source_quote: the first frame to be received from either network with the next valid sequence number is accepted and passed up the stack to the receiving partition. When the second frame is received with this sequence number, it is simply discarded.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by accepting duplicate frames or rejecting the first valid frame.

rules.name: Sequence Number Addition

constraint.value: A sequence number must be added to each frame per Virtual Link (VL) to enable ordered stream reconstruction without duplication.

rules.source_quote: Here a sequence number field is added to each frame, and the sequence numbers are incremented on each successive frame.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by omitting the sequence number or using an invalid format.

rules.name: Initial Sequence Number
rules.source_quote: For each VL, the sequence number should initially be set to 0.
rules.source_section: 3.2.6.1 Sequence Numbers and the Sending End System
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by initializing the sequence number to a value other than 0.

rules.name: Sequence Number Reset on ES Reset

constraint.value: The sequence number must be reset to 0 following a reset of the transmitting End System (ES).

rules.source_quote: The sequence number is always assigned this initial value following a reset of the transmitting ES.
rules.source_section: 3.2.6.1 Sequence Numbers and the Sending End System
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by not resetting the sequence number after an ES reset.

rules.name: Sequence Number Increment and Wrap-Around

constraint.value: The sequence number must be incremented by one for each consecutive frame of the same VL and wrap around to 1 after reaching 255.

rules.source_quote: The frame sequence number should be incremented by one for each consecutive frame of the same VL and wrap-around to 1 following the value 255.
rules.source_section: 3.2.6.1 Sequence Numbers and the Sending End System
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by skipping sequence numbers, not incrementing, or wrapping around incorrectly (e.g., to 0 instead of 1).

rules.name: Redundancy Management Placement

constraint.value: Redundancy Management (RM) must be placed after Integrity Checking (IC) in the receive path.

rules.source_quote: RM (Redundancy Management) is placed after IC (Integrity Checking).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by simulating RM before IC or omitting IC entirely.

rules.name: Redundant Frame Elimination

constraint.value: Redundancy Management must eliminate frames that are redundant copies of frames already passed to the partition.

rules.source_quote: The function of the AFDX redundancy management is merely to eliminate frames that are redundant copies of frames that it has already passed on to the partition.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by forwarding duplicate frames to the partition.

rules.name: Abnormal Frame Handling

constraint.value: Abnormal frames must not be forwarded to the partition.

rules.source_quote: Redundancy management result: abnormal frame is not forwarded to partition.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by forwarding abnormal frames to the partition.

rules.name: Frame Loss Handling

constraint.value: If a frame is lost on one network, the frame arriving on the redundant network must be accepted.

rules.source_quote: Redundancy management result: The frame arriving on the B Network is accepted.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by rejecting the frame from the redundant network when the primary frame is lost.

rules.name: Babbling Switch Handling

constraint.value: Frames from a babbling switch (stuck frame) must not be forwarded to the IP layer due to Integrity Checking.

rules.source_quote: In example 4 the Redundancy Management result is that frames are not forwarded to the IP layer due to Integrity Checking.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could violate this by forwarding frames from a babbling switch to the IP layer.

rules.name: Sequence number location in frame

constraint.value: Located just before the MAC CRC field, as part of the MAC payload

rules.source_quote: The frame sequence number should be located just before the MAC CRC field, as part of the MAC payload, as illustrated in Figure 3-19.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with the sequence number misplaced (e.g., in the AFDX payload or after the CRC) to test if the receiving End System discards them.

rules.name: Maximum time difference between redundant frame copies
rules.source_quote: In order to simplify the algorithm on the receiving End System, redundant copies of a frame should be sent within a maximum time difference of 0.5 ms.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate redundant frames with a time difference exceeding 0.5 ms to test if the receiving End System handles them correctly (e.g., discards or flags them).

rules.name: Redundancy per Virtual Link configurability
rules.source_quote: On a per VL basis, the ES should be able to send messages on either or both networks. This property should be configurable.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames on both networks for a VL configured as non-redundant, or on only one network for a VL configured as redundant, to test enforcement.

rules.name: Valid sequence number interval for received frames

constraint.value: [PSN+1, PSN+2] (with wrap-around)

rules.source_quote: For each network the Integrity Checking tests each frame for a sequence number in the interval: [PSN+1, PSN+2] Where Previous Sequence Number (PSN) is the sequence number of the previous frame received (but not necessarily forwarded) on this VL. The operator '+' takes the wrap-around of Sequence Numbers into account.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with sequence numbers outside the [PSN+1, PSN+2] range (e.g., PSN+3 or PSN-1) to test if the Integrity Checking discards them.

rules.name: Acceptance of sequence number 0

constraint.value: Accept frames with sequence number 0 as valid

rules.source_quote: The Integrity Checking should also accept the frame as valid in the following special cases: • The Received Sequence Number (RSN) is equal to 0
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with sequence number 0 to test if they are accepted, even if not following the [PSN+1, PSN+2] rule.

rules.name: Acceptance of first frame after reset

constraint.value: Accept the first frame received after any reset of the receiving ES as valid

rules.source_quote: The Integrity Checking should also accept the frame as valid in the following special cases: • The frame is the first frame received after any reset of the receiving ES
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a reset of the receiving ES and send a frame with an arbitrary sequence number to test if it is accepted.

rules.name: Integrity checking disablement per VL
rules.source_quote: It should be possible on a per VL basis to disable the integrity checking on both networks through the configuration table.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with invalid sequence numbers for a VL with integrity checking disabled to test if they are accepted.

rules.name: SkewMax parameter per VL

constraint.value: Depends on network topology; provided by system integrator

rules.source_quote: RM configuration is generally based on the SkewMax parameter: i.e. the maximum time between the reception of two redundant frames. This value depends on the network topology (number of switches crossed by the frames) and should be provided by the system integrator.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate redundant frames with a time difference exceeding the configured SkewMax value to test if the Redundancy Management discards or flags them.

rules.name: Redundant VL frame delivery

value: deliver one of the redundant data (RM active)
deliver both redundant data (RM not active)

rules.source_quote: On a per VL basis, the ES should be able to receive: • A redundant VL and deliver to the partition one of the redundant data (RM active) • A redundant VL and deliver to the partition both redundant data (RM not active)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send redundant frames and observe if the receiving ES delivers one or both copies based on RM configuration.

rules.name: Non-redundant VL frame delivery

constraint.value: Submit data from the non-redundant VL to the partition, regardless of RM status

rules.source_quote: • A non redundant VL on either interface and submit data from it to the partition (in this case, RM can be active or not)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames on a non-redundant VL and verify that the receiving ES always delivers them to the partition.

rules.name: First Win Redundancy Policy

constraint.value: Deliver the first of the redundant frames received

rules.source_quote: When redundancy management is active, it should deliver the first of the redundant frames received.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send two redundant frames with identical RSN but different payloads or arrival times to test if the first received is always delivered.

rules.name: Reset Independence of Redundancy Management

constraint.value: Reset of transmitting/receiving End System or AFDX switch must not affect the 'First Win' property

rules.source_quote: Reset of any equipment involved in the communication (transmitting End system, receiving End system or the AFDX switch) should not affect this property.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a reset event during frame transmission and verify if the first received frame is still delivered correctly.

rules.name: Hardware Reset Time vs SkewMax

constraint.value: Hardware reset time must be larger than SkewMax

rules.source_quote: The hardware reset time is assumed to be larger than SkewMax.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a reset time shorter than SkewMax and observe if RM algorithm is disturbed by pre-reset frames.

rules.name: RSN-Only Rejection Criterion

constraint.value: Use only the RSN (Redundancy Sequence Number) for frame rejection or acceptance

rules.source_quote: The Redundancy Management Algorithm should only use the RSN of a frame as the criterion for rejection or acceptance.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with valid RSN but invalid integrity checks to test if RM ignores integrity for acceptance.

rules.name: Increasing RSN Order Requirement

constraint.value: Frames must be forwarded in increasing RSN order for each VL at the receiver

rules.source_quote: For each VL at the receiver, the Redundancy Management (RM) function should ensure that frames are forwarded in an increasing RSN order.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with out-of-order RSN (e.g., RSN 3 before RSN 2) to test if RM enforces ordering.

rules.name: SkewMax Exceeded Frame Acceptance

constraint.value: If SkewMax is exceeded after reception of a frame, accept the next frame regardless of its RSN

rules.source_quote: If skew max is exceeded after the reception of a frame, RM will accept the next frame whatever its sequence number is.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could delay a frame beyond SkewMax and send a subsequent frame with an arbitrary RSN to test acceptance.

rules.name: In-Sequence Frame Forwarding

constraint.value: Forward only in-sequence frames; reordering is not required

rules.source_quote: The Redundancy Management function must forward only in-sequence frames, but reordering is not required.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames out of sequence and observe if RM drops or forwards them incorrectly.

rules.name: Redundant Frame Loss Due to Network Asymmetry

constraint.value: Loss of one frame on one network may lead to loss of its copy on the redundant network

rules.source_quote: In some cases, the loss of one frame on one network could also lead to the loss of its copy.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate asymmetric frame loss (e.g., drop frame on Network A but not its copy on Network B) and observe if RM drops the copy.

rules.name: Port Transmit or Receive Only
rules.source_quote: A user port is configured to either transmit or receive, but not both.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could configure a port to both transmit and receive, violating the exclusivity rule.

rules.name: No Shared Transmit Ports
rules.source_quote: Having two data sources for one transmit AFDX com or SAP port may also result in a loss of data... The examples with red cross should not be used.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate two data sources transmitting to the same AFDX port, violating the no-sharing rule.

rules.name: Sampling Message Size Constraint
rules.source_quote: Sampling Com Ports should not use IP fragmentation, therefore the size of each sampling message should be less than or equal to the payload size of the associated Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate a sampling message larger than the VL payload size, violating the size constraint.

rules.name: Sampling Service Communication Type
rules.source_quote: Sampling service should be based on multicast and unidirectional communication to send data from one source to one or several receptors.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a bidirectional or unicast-only sampling service, violating the multicast/unidirectional rule.

rules.name: Sampling Service Connectionless
rules.source_quote: The sampling service is simple, connectionless without acknowledge.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a connection-oriented sampling service, violating the connectionless rule.

rules.name: Sampling Port Multi-Partition Read

constraint.value: multiple_partitions_can_read

rules.source_quote: The last message stored in a particular sampling port should be able to be read by several partitions (i.e. several partitions may subscribe to this sampling port).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could restrict sampling port access to a single partition, violating the multi-partition read rule.

rules.name: Sampling Port Freshness Indication
rules.source_quote: A freshness indication should be associated to each sampling port. This freshness indication should be available to each partition reading the message.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could omit freshness indication in sampling port messages, violating the freshness rule.

rules.name: Queuing Service Connectionless
rules.source_quote: The queuing service is simple, connectionless, without acknowledgement.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a connection-oriented queuing service, violating the connectionless rule.

rules.name: Queuing Service Variable Message Size
rules.source_quote: The queuing service should be able to manage messages of different sizes for the same queuing Communication Port.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could enforce fixed message sizes for a queuing port, violating the variable size rule.

rules.name: Queuing Service FIFO Discipline
rules.source_quote: To guarantee the sequence of messages, the queuing service should manage the messages with FIFO discipline in transmission and reception.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could reorder queuing messages, violating the FIFO discipline rule.

rules.name: Queuing Service Max Application Data Size
rules.source_quote: Each instance of Queuing Service should be able to manage up to 8 k octets of application data (IP fragmentation is thus needed).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate queuing messages exceeding 8 kB of application data, violating the size limit.

rules.name: Queuing Fragment Transmission Order

constraint.value: in_order_transmission

rules.source_quote: When fragmentation is used, the fragments should be transmitted in-order to the AFDX network.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could reorder fragments during transmission, violating the in-order rule.

rules.name: Queuing Buffer Overflow Handling

constraint.value: discard_and_notify

rules.source_quote: If a buffer overflow occurs in transmission, an error indication should be sent to the transmitting partition and the frame should be discarded.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a buffer overflow without discarding the frame or notifying the partition, violating the handling rule.

rules.name: Reassembly before delivery to partition

constraint.value: No data shall be presented to a partition in the queuing services FIFO until the whole message has been reassembled.

rules.source_quote: In case of fragmentation, no data should be presented to a partition in the queuing services FIFO until whole message has been reassembled.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send fragmented frames out of order or with missing fragments to test if the receiver delivers partial data to the partition.

rules.name: Reception buffer overflow handling

constraint.value: If a buffer overflow occurs in reception, an error message shall be sent to the receiving partition and the frame shall be discarded.

rules.source_quote: If a buffer overflow occurs in reception, an error message should be sent to the receiving partition and the frame should be discarded.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could flood the receiver with frames to trigger buffer overflow and verify error message generation and frame discarding.

rules.name: UDP SAP port payload size limit
rules.source_quote: Each instance of the UDP Service Access Point should handle up to 8k octets.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send UDP frames with payloads exceeding 8192 octets to test SAP port handling.

rules.name: SAP port receiver buffer overflow handling

constraint.value: If receiver buffer overflow occurs in a SAP port, an error message shall be sent to the receiving partition and the frame shall be discarded.

rules.source_quote: If receiver buffer overflow occurs, an error message is sent to the receiving partition, and the frame should be discarded.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could overload a SAP port receiver buffer to verify error message generation and frame discarding.

rules.name: TFTP block size limit
rules.source_quote: Each instance of File Transfer service should be able to manage up to 8 k octets blocks.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send TFTP blocks larger than 8192 octets to test block size enforcement.

rules.name: Sub-VL FIFO queue limit per VL
rules.source_quote: A VL FIFO queue should be able to manage at most 4 Sub-VL FIFO queues.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could configure a VL with more than 4 Sub-VL FIFO queues to test limit enforcement.

rules.name: Sub-VL round-robin scheduling

constraint.value: Sub-VL FIFO queues shall be read in round-robin sequence such that if any Sub-VL FIFO queue has traffic, one frame per BAG is sent to the main VL. Once a frame is sent, the sequence is halted until the BAG ends and the sequence is then restarted with the next Sub-VL FIFO queue.

rules.source_quote: Each Sub-VF FIFO queue should be read in round-robin sequence such that if any Sub-VF FIFO queue has traffic, one frame per BAG is sent to the main VL. Once a frame is sent, the sequence is halted until the BAG ends and the sequence is then restarted with the next Sub-VF FIFO queue.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames to Sub-VLs out of round-robin order or violate BAG timing to test scheduling enforcement.

rules.name: Sub-VL FIFO exclusivity

constraint.value: A Sub-VL FIFO queue shall only be read by one VL FIFO queue.

rules.source_quote: A Sub-VL FIFO queue should only be read by one VL FIFO queue.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to associate a Sub-VL FIFO with multiple VL FIFO queues to test exclusivity.

rules.name: IP fragmentation at IP layer

constraint.value: IP fragmentation shall be performed at the IP layer, if needed.

rules.source_quote: IP fragmentation should be performed at the IP layer, if it is needed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject fragmented frames at the Sub-VL layer to test if fragmentation is rejected or handled incorrectly.

rules.name: Round-robin with fragmentation

constraint.value: The round robin shall continue in the presence of IP fragmentation so that one fragment is fetched from one Sub-VL, and then a frame or fragment is taken from the following Sub-VL.

rules.source_quote: The round robin continues in the presence of IP fragmentation so that one fragment is fetched from one Sub-VL, and then a frame or fragment is taken from the following Sub-VL.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could interleave fragments from different Sub-VLs to test round-robin enforcement during fragmentation.

rules.name: Sub-VL layering

constraint.value: Sub-VLs shall be below the IP layer.

rules.source_quote: Sub-VLs are below the IP layer.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject IP-layer traffic directly into Sub-VLs to test layering enforcement.

rules.name: Full-duplex Ethernet compliance
rules.source_quote: The Data-link layer of the ES should be based on the use of Full-duplex Ethernet links as defined in IEEE 802.3 standard.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames using half-duplex Ethernet settings or non-IEEE 802.3 compliant frames.

rules.name: IEEE 802.3 frame compliance

constraint.value: compliant_with_IEEE_802.3

rules.source_quote: Any Ethernet Frame generated by the End System should be compliant with IEEE 802.3 standard.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate malformed Ethernet frames (e.g., incorrect preamble, invalid FCS, or non-standard frame lengths).

rules.name: Continuous transmission on link failure
rules.source_quote: All output interfaces will continue to transmit, even in the case of a physical layer link failure.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a link failure and verify if the End System stops transmitting frames (violation).

rules.name: Per-VL maximum frame length
rules.source_quote: A maximum AFDX frame length should be defined on a per VL basis.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames exceeding the configured maximum length for a specific VL.

rules.name: Frame forwarding to upper layer

constraint.value: valid_AFDX_format_and_FCS_and_CRC

rules.source_quote: In reception, if the AFDX frame format and Frame Check Sequence (FCS) and Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) are valid (without preamble and Start Frame Delimiter fields) the frame should be forwarded to the upper layer.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with invalid FCS, CRC, or malformed AFDX headers to test forwarding behavior.

rules.name: IP version compliance
rules.source_quote: The packet structure version should be IPv4.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate IPv6 packets or malformed IPv4 headers.

rules.name: IPv4 total length range
rules.source_quote: Ordinarily, in the IPv4 packet structure, the Total Length field should range from 21 to 1500 bytes. In AFDX, this range is from 21 to 1499 due to the Sequence Number (see Section 3.2.6.2.2, Redundancy Management Function).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate IPv4 packets with Total Length outside the 21-1499 byte range.

rules.name: Unique data flow identification

constraint.value: UDP_TCP_dest_port + IP_dest_address + MAC_dest_address + physical_Ethernet_connection

rules.source_quote: A data flow is uniquely identified within AFDX network by the set of UDP/TCP destination port, IP destination address, MAC destination address and the physical Ethernet connection(s) of the receiving ES.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with duplicate or conflicting data flow identifiers to test uniqueness enforcement.

rules.name: Frame filtering by destination addresses

constraint.value: destination_TCP_UDP_port + destination_IP_address + destination_MAC_address + physical_Ethernet_connection

rules.source_quote: Frame based filtering is done such that the receiving End System will only forward valid frames to a communication or a SAP port. Valid frame being defined by analysis of destination (TCP/UDP, IP, MAC) addresses and physical Ethernet connections.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with mismatched or invalid destination addresses to test filtering behavior.

rules.name: Static Transmit Table Configuration

constraint.value: Each entry in the transmit table must statically define the source AFDX port, source partition, source UDP port, source IP, source MAC, destination UDP port, destination IP, and destination MAC (VL).

rules.source_quote: The following tables show the address tables for each ES: Transmit Table of End-System 1: Src AFDX Communication Port, Src partition, Src UDP, Src IP, Src MAC, Dest UDP, Dest IP, Dest MAC (VL1).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with mismatched or undefined entries in the transmit table (e.g., incorrect source/destination IP, UDP port, or MAC address).

rules.name: Static Receive Table Configuration

constraint.value: Each entry in the receive table must statically define the destination AFDX port(s), destination partition(s), source UDP port, source IP, source MAC, destination UDP port, destination IP, and destination MAC (VL).

rules.source_quote: Receive Table of End-System 2: Dest AFDX Communication Port(s), Dest partition(s), Src UDP, Src IP, Src MAC, Dest UDP, Dest IP, Dest MAC (VL1).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with mismatched or undefined entries in the receive table (e.g., incorrect source/destination IP, UDP port, or MAC address).

rules.name: Receiver Demultiplexing Based on Address Fields
rules.source_quote: At the receiver, the demultiplexing is based only on the MAC, IP, UDP destination address.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with incorrect or mismatched MAC, IP, or UDP destination addresses to test demultiplexing logic.

rules.name: Static Switch Forwarding Based on MAC Destination

constraint.value: Switch forwarding must be statically defined based on the MAC destination field of received frames, mapping input ports to output ports.

rules.source_quote: Table 3-2 – Switch Forwarding: Input port, MAC destination field of the received frames, Output ports.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with incorrect or undefined MAC destination addresses to test switch forwarding logic.

rules.name: Unique Message Identification Quintuplet
rules.source_quote: Peer-to-peer communications are identified in each frame by UDP Source Port + Source IP + Destination MAC (VL identification) + Destination IP + UDP Destination Port as illustrated in Figure 3-34.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with duplicate or mismatched quintuplets to test uniqueness enforcement.

rules.name: Unique Quintuplet per Message

constraint.value: Each message must be uniquely identified by a distinct quintuplet (UDP Source Port, Source IP, Destination MAC, Destination IP, UDP Destination Port).

rules.source_quote: In the AFDX network, this quintuplet provides a unique identification for each message.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with duplicate quintuplets to test uniqueness validation.

rules.name: Static Addressing for Intra-AFDX Communication

constraint.value: For Intra-AFDX communication, the addressing (quintuplet) must be statically defined for each message.

rules.source_quote: The principal characteristic of Intra-AFDX communication is the fact that for each message, the addressing is statically defined.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with dynamic or mismatched addressing for Intra-AFDX communication.

rules.name: UDP Port Usage for AFDX Communication Ports

constraint.value: AFDX communication ports must be defined through UDP ports, which can be either transmitters or receivers.

rules.source_quote: AFDX communication ports are defined through UDP ports. Such ports can be either transmitters or receivers.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with invalid or undefined UDP ports for AFDX communication ports.

rules.name: Queuing Mode for Bi-Directional Communication

constraint.value: For bi-directional communication using conventional AFDX communication ports, the ports must be used in queuing mode.

rules.source_quote: For a bi-directional communication, the ports should be used in queuing mode.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames for bi-directional communication using ports not configured in queuing mode.

rules.name: Static Quintuplet for Unidirectional Extra-AFDX Communication

constraint.value: For unidirectional Extra-AFDX communication, the ES configuration table must contain a statically defined quintuplet for addressing (destination IP and port number).

rules.source_quote: The implication is that the ES configuration table will contain the destination IP and port number. Hence there will be a statically defined quintuplet for addressing.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with dynamic or mismatched quintuplets for Extra-AFDX unidirectional communication.

rules.name: IP_Unicast_Address_Structure
rules.source_quote: IP Unicast Addressing Format (source or unicast destination) 32-bits: Class A, 1-bit Private IP address, 7-bits User_Defined_ID, 16-bits Partition ID, 3-bits Spare field, 5-bits (constant '0001010').
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with malformed IP unicast addresses, e.g., incorrect bit lengths for User_Defined_ID or Partition_ID, or non-zero spare field when not required.

rules.name: IP_Unicast_Spare_Field_Usage
rules.source_quote: The Spare field is normally not used and set to zero as shown in Figure 3-37.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with non-zero values in the spare field (e.g., 1, 2, 4, or 7).

rules.name: IP_Multicast_Address_Structure
rules.source_quote: IP Multicast Addressing Format: 32 bits, 4 bits Class D '1110', 12 bits constant field '000011100000', 16 bits Virtual Link Identifier.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with malformed IP multicast addresses, e.g., incorrect Class D bits, altered constant field, or invalid Virtual Link Identifier.

rules.name: AFDX_Communication_Port_Unidirectional_Access
rules.source_quote: Unidirectional access: Transmission (Tx) or reception (Rx).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can simulate an AFDX Communication Port attempting bidirectional access (e.g., transmitting and receiving on the same port).

rules.name: AFDX_Communication_Port_Transmit_Quintuplet_Uniqueness

constraint.value: unique_per_port

rules.source_quote: In transmission, there is only one link between 'AFDX Communication port' and the quintuplet (UDP Source Port, Source IP, destination Mac, destination IP, UDP destination port).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where a single AFDX Communication Port is linked to multiple quintuplets (e.g., varying UDP source ports or destination IPs).

rules.name: AFDX_Communication_Port_Receive_Quintuplet_Uniqueness

constraint.value: unique_per_port

rules.source_quote: In reception, there is only one link between 'AFDX Communication port' and the quintuplet (UDP Source Port, Source IP, destination Mac, destination IP, UDP destination port).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where a single AFDX Communication Port is linked to multiple receive quintuplets (e.g., varying UDP destination ports or source IPs).

rules.name: AFDX_Communication_Port_Transmit_Configuration_Frozen

constraint.value: frozen_by_configuration

rules.source_quote: The transmission and the reception path is frozen by configuration.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where the transmit configuration (e.g., UDP source port or destination IP) is dynamically altered during operation.

rules.name: AFDX_Communication_Port_Transmit_Link_Constraint

constraint.value: single_set_per_port

rules.source_quote: In transmission, an AFDX Communication Port should only be linked to a single set UDP port source, IP source, VL (MAC destination), IP destination and UDP destination.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where an AFDX Communication Port is linked to multiple sets of (UDP source port, IP source, VL, IP destination, UDP destination).

rules.name: AFDX_Communication_Port_Receive_Link_Constraint

constraint.value: single_set_per_port

rules.source_quote: In reception, an AFDX Communication Port should only be linked to a single set (unique UDP port destination, IP destination, VL (MAC destination)) and additionally to the Ethernet physical interface if the redundancy management is disabling.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where an AFDX Communication Port is linked to multiple sets of (UDP destination port, IP destination, VL).

rules.name: SAP_Port_Unidirectional_Access
rules.source_quote: Unidirectional access: Transmission or reception.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can simulate a SAP Port attempting bidirectional access (e.g., transmitting and receiving on the same port).

rules.name: SAP_Port_Transmit_Quadruplet_Configuration

constraint.value: frozen_by_configuration

rules.source_quote: In transmission, the SAP port uses by configuration a frozen quadruplet (UDP Port source address, IP source address, Mac Source address, MAC destination address (VL identification)).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where the transmit quadruplet (e.g., UDP source port or MAC destination) is dynamically altered during operation.

rules.name: SAP Port Transmission Uniqueness

constraint.value: A SAP Port in transmission must be linked to only one unique set of (UDP source port, IP source address, VL (MAC destination))

rules.source_quote: In transmission, a SAP Port should only be linked to a single set (UDP port source, IP source and VL (MAC destination)).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where a SAP Port is linked to multiple (UDP source port, IP source, VL) sets in transmission.

rules.name: SAP Port Reception Uniqueness

constraint.value: A SAP Port in reception must be linked to only one unique set of (UDP/TCP destination port, IP destination address, VL (MAC destination))

rules.source_quote: In reception, a SAP Port should only be linked to a single set (UDP/TCP port destination, IP destination and VL (MAC destination)).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where a SAP Port is linked to multiple (UDP/TCP destination port, IP destination, VL) sets in reception.

rules.name: UDP/TCP Port Number as Service Access Point Identifier

constraint.value: The UDP/TCP port number must identify the Service Access Point (SAP).

rules.source_quote: The UDP/TCP port number should identify the Service Access Point.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where the UDP/TCP port number does not correspond to any defined SAP.

rules.name: Reception Availability of IP and UDP/TCP Source

constraint.value: In reception, the Service Access Point must make the IP source address and UDP/TCP source port available to the receiving partition.

rules.source_quote: In reception, the Service Access Point should make available the IP source and the UDP/TCP Source to the receiving partition.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where the IP source or UDP/TCP source port is not made available to the receiving partition.

rules.name: Transmission Specification of Destination IP and UDP/TCP Port

constraint.value: In transmission, the Service Access Point must permit the partition to specify the IP destination address and UDP/TCP destination port.

rules.source_quote: In transmission, the Service Access Point should permit the partition to specify the IP address and the UDP/TCP port of the destination partition.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where the partition is not allowed to specify the IP destination or UDP/TCP destination port.

rules.name: AFDX Communication Port Range for Sampling and Queuing
rules.source_quote: AFDX Communication port AFDX Ù AFDX AFDX Ù Compliant network 1 024 – 65 535 Used for sampling and queuing communications
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with AFDX communication port numbers outside the range 1024–65535 for sampling and queuing.

rules.name: AFDX Communication Port Range for Standard Communications
rules.source_quote: AFDX Ù AFDX AFDX ÙCompliant network 0 – 1023 Used for standard communications e.g Port 69 to open a TFTP, Data loading (ARINC 615A), SNMP, etc..
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with AFDX communication port numbers outside the range 0–1023 for standard communications.

rules.name: SAP Port Range for Bi-directional Communication
rules.source_quote: SAP AFDX Ù AFDX AFDX ÙCompliant network 1 024 – 65 535 Used for bi-directional communication: specific TFTP etc..,
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate SAP frames with port numbers outside the range 1024–65535 for bi-directional communication.

rules.name: Port Number Uniqueness within Virtual Link

constraint.value: Two identical port numbers cannot be used within the same Virtual Link.

rules.source_quote: the only technical limitation regarding port number duplication is that two identical port number cannot be used with in a Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with duplicate port numbers within the same Virtual Link.

rules.name: Switch Filtering and Policing Function Existence

constraint.value: All frames arriving at the switch must pass through the Filtering & Policing function stage for validation.

rules.source_quote: All frames arrive at the switch in the Filtering & Policing function stage where they are filtered in various steps that apply rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget and acceptable destination(s).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can bypass the Filtering & Policing function in the switch simulation to test enforcement.

rules.name: Switch Filtering Rules Enforcement

constraint.value: The Filtering & Policing function must enforce rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget, and acceptable destination(s).

rules.source_quote: All frames arrive at the switch in the Filtering & Policing function stage where they are filtered in various steps that apply rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget and acceptable destination(s).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames that violate frame integrity, length, traffic budget, or destination rules to test enforcement.

rules.name: Switching Function Core Activity

constraint.value: Frames filtered by the Filtering and Policing function must be forwarded to the appropriate physical output ports.

rules.source_quote: The core of the switching activity is performed by the Switching function. Frames filtered by the Filtering and Policing function are forwarded to the appropriate physical output ports where they leave the switch again.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames that are not forwarded to the correct output ports despite passing filtering.

rules.name: Switch Configuration Tables Static Data

constraint.value: Switch operations must be controlled by static configuration data contained in Configuration Tables.

rules.source_quote: These functions are controlled by configuration data contained in static Configuration Tables.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can modify or corrupt the static configuration tables to test switch behavior.

rules.name: Switch Monitoring Function Events and Statistics

constraint.value: The Monitoring function must log events such as frame arrival and failed CRC checks, and create statistics about the internal situation.

rules.source_quote: All operations are monitored by a Monitoring function that logs events such as the arrival of a frame or a failed CRC check and additionally creates statistics about the internal situation.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames that trigger events (e.g., failed CRC) and verify if the Monitoring function logs them correctly.

rules.name: Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAG) definition

constraint.value: BAGi represents the minimum interval between the start of consecutive frames for Virtual Link VLi (expressed in seconds)

rules.source_quote: The BAG (Bandwidth Allocation Gap) associated to VLi is BAGi (expressed in seconds)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames for the same VL with intervals shorter than BAGi.

rules.name: Jitter definition for Virtual Link

constraint.value: Ji,switch represents the maximum jitter (window) within which a frame for VLi is assured to be located when entering a switch (expressed in seconds)

rules.source_quote: The Jitter (representing the Window a frame is assured to be located within) associated to VLi entering a particular switch is Ji,switch (expressed in seconds)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by introducing jitter exceeding Ji,switch for a given VL.

rules.name: Maximum frame size for Virtual Link
rules.source_quote: The maximum frame size for VLi is denoted Si max (expressed in bytes). Si max is a configurable parameter that should be in the range [84, 1538]
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames larger than Si_max for a given VL.

rules.name: Minimum frame size for Virtual Link
rules.source_quote: The minimum frame size for VLi is denoted Si min (expressed in bytes). Si min is a configurable parameter that should be in the range [84, 1538]. Si min should be less than or equal to Si max
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames smaller than Si_min for a given VL.

rules.name: Minimum Ethernet frame size (MAC level)
rules.source_quote: Ethernet frame size (L) in the range [64 octets, 1518 octets]
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending Ethernet frames smaller than 64 octets or larger than 1518 octets.

rules.name: Maximum Ethernet frame size (MAC level)
rules.source_quote: Ethernet frame size (L) in the range [64 octets, 1518 octets]
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending Ethernet frames larger than 1518 octets.

rules.name: Frame size compliance with VL maximum

constraint.value: Ethernet frame size (L) must be less than or equal to Lmax for the VL

rules.source_quote: Ethernet frame size (L) less that or equal to Lmax
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames with L > Lmax for a given VL.

rules.name: Frame size compliance with VL minimum (byte-based policing)

constraint.value: Ethernet frame size (S) must be greater than or equal to Smin for the VL when byte-based traffic policing is used

rules.source_quote: Ethernet frame size (S) greater than or equal to Smin, only in case where byte-based traffic policing is used
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames with S < Smin for a VL configured with byte-based policing.

rules.name: Frame size envelope validation

constraint.value: Frames must not be longer or shorter than the allowed envelope (Smin ≤ S ≤ Smax or Lmin ≤ L ≤ Lmax)

rules.source_quote: The frame size: whether the frame is either longer or shorter than the envelope allows
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames outside the allowed size envelope for a VL.

rules.name: Frame Check Sequence (FCS) validity

constraint.value: FCS embedded in the frame must match the calculation upon reception

rules.source_quote: The frame integrity: whether the FCS embedded in the frame matches the calculation upon reception
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by corrupting the FCS field in the frame.

rules.name: Destination address validity (VL mapping)

constraint.value: Destination Address must correspond to a valid VL (including constant field)

rules.source_quote: Destination address validity (Ethernet Address corresponds to a valid VL, including constant field)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames with an invalid or unmapped Destination Address.

rules.name: VL reception port validity

constraint.value: VL must be valid to be received on the destination port (according to switch configuration table)

rules.source_quote: This VL is valid to be received on that destination port (according to the switch configuration table)
