rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending a frame for a VL to a port not configured to receive it.

rules.name: Ethernet frame octet alignment

constraint.value: Ethernet frame size (L) must be an integral number of octets

rules.source_quote: Ethernet frame size (L) is an integral number of octets (alignment)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by sending frames with non-integral octet sizes (e.g., 65.5 octets).

rules.name: Byte-based traffic policing

constraint.value: Byte-based policing filters VL traffic based on bandwidth usage expressed in bits per second

rules.source_quote: The byte-based traffic policing filters out the VL in terms of bandwidth usage expressed in bits per second
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by exceeding the bandwidth limit (bits per second) for a VL configured with byte-based policing.

rules.name: Frame-based traffic policing

constraint.value: Frame-based policing filters VL traffic based on bandwidth usage expressed in frames per second

rules.source_quote: The frame-based traffic policing filters out the VL in terms of bandwidth usage expressed in frames per second
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can violate this by exceeding the frame rate limit (frames per second) for a VL configured with frame-based policing.

rules.name: Discard of non-compliant frames

constraint.value: Frames that do not comply with configuration parameters must be discarded (filtered) and MIB entries updated

rules.source_quote: If the frame properties do not comply with the configuration parameters, the frame is filtered i.e. discarded, and one or more MIB entries updated
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can observe if non-compliant frames are discarded and MIB entries are updated accordingly.

rules.name: Token Bucket Initialization (No Jitter)

constraint.value: ACi = S_i_max

rules.source_quote: If Ji,switch=0, then ACi is set initially to S i max (see Figure 4-4).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with an initial ACi value not equal to S_i_max when jitter is zero, violating the initialization rule.

rules.name: Token Bucket Credit Accumulation Rate

constraint.value: ACi credited proportionally to S_i_max / BAG_i

rules.source_quote: ACi is credited as time elapses, proportionally to S i max with an upper limit of BAG i
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate incorrect credit accumulation rates (e.g., faster or slower than S_i_max / BAG_i).

rules.name: Token Bucket Upper Limit

constraint.value: ACi <= BAG_i

rules.source_quote: ACi is credited as time elapses, proportionally to S i max with an upper limit of BAG i
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames that cause ACi to exceed BAG_i, violating the upper limit constraint.

rules.name: Byte-Based Policing Acceptance Condition

constraint.value: Byte_ACi >= S

rules.source_quote: If Byte ACi is greater than S, the frame is accepted and Byte ACi is debited by S
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames when Byte_ACi < S, causing the switch to incorrectly accept them.

rules.name: Byte-Based Policing Rejection Condition

constraint.value: Byte_ACi < S

rules.source_quote: If Byte ACi is less than S, the frame is discarded, the appropriate MIB entry is updated and Byte ACi is not changed
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames when Byte_ACi >= S, causing the switch to incorrectly discard them.

rules.name: Frame-Based Policing Acceptance Condition

constraint.value: Frame_ACi >= S_i_max

rules.source_quote: If Frame ACi is greater than S i max, the frame is accepted and Frame ACi is debited by S i max
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames when Frame_ACi < S_i_max, causing the switch to incorrectly accept them.

rules.name: Frame-Based Policing Rejection Condition

constraint.value: Frame_ACi < S_i_max

rules.source_quote: If Frame ACi is less than S i max, the frame is discarded, the appropriate MIB entry is updated and Frame ACi is not changed
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames when Frame_ACi >= S_i_max, causing the switch to incorrectly discard them.

rules.name: Budget Account Non-Consumption for Invalid Frames
rules.source_quote: Budget Accounts (Bytes ACi and Frame ACi) should not be consumed by invalid frames, i.e. frames not forwarded by the forwarding function.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate invalid frames (e.g., corrupted CRC) and verify that ACi is not debited.

rules.name: CRC Validation Requirement
rules.source_quote: The Switch should test each frame by use of the Frame Check Sequence (CRC) field according to IEEE Std 802.3. The Switch should discard Frames that do not satisfy this test.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with invalid CRC values to test if the switch discards them.

rules.name: Ethernet Frame Size Limits
rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming Ethernet frames having an Ethernet frame size (L) greater than 1518 or less than 64 bytes.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with sizes < 64 bytes or > 1518 bytes to test if the switch discards them.

rules.name: Policing Algorithm Choice
rules.source_quote: The switch may implement one of the two algorithm, either Byte-based or Frame-based, or both of them.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic that violates the expected behavior of the chosen policing algorithm (e.g., byte-based vs. frame-based).

rules.name: Total Ethernet Line Size Calculation
rules.source_quote: Let s be the total Ethernet line size of the received frame (S = Ethernet frame size (L) + 20 octets; the 20 octets correspond to IFG+Preamble+SFD).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with incorrect S values (e.g., not equal to L + 20).

rules.name: Discard frames with non-integral octet size

constraint.value: must be an integral number of octets

rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames having an Ethernet frame size that is not an integral number of octets (alignment errors).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with odd byte counts (e.g., 65 bytes) and verify they are discarded by the switch.

rules.name: Discard frames exceeding maximum size (Lmax) for VL
rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames which total Ethernet line size is greater than the maximum size (Lmax) allowed for the relevant VL, as such a frame would consume more bandwidth than allocated.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames larger than the configured Lmax for a VL and verify they are discarded.

rules.name: Discard frames smaller than minimum size (Smin) for VL (byte-based policing)
rules.source_quote: In the case where byte-based policing is used, the switch should also discard incoming frames which total Ethernet line size is smaller than the minimum size (Smin) allowed for the relevant VL.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames smaller than the configured Smin for a VL (if byte-based policing is enabled) and verify they are discarded.

rules.name: Discard frames with erroneous 32-bit constant in MAC destination address

constraint.value: must not contain an erroneous 32-bit constant field

rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames with a MAC destination address that has an erroneous 32-bit constant field.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with an invalid 32-bit constant in the MAC destination address and verify they are discarded.

rules.name: Discard frames with disallowed VL ID on incoming port

constraint.value: must be allowed on the incoming port

rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames for which the VL id is not allowed on the incoming port.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with a VL ID not configured for the incoming port and verify they are discarded.

rules.name: Use VL identifier to access filtering and policing parameters

constraint.value: must be used to obtain filtering and policing parameters from the configuration table

rules.source_quote: The switch should use the VL identifier to obtain the appropriate information of filtering and policing from the configuration table.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with a VL ID not present in the configuration table and verify policing behavior.

rules.name: Support one-to-one or one-to-many MAC destination to account mapping

value: one ACi for one MAC destination address (VLi)
one ACi for a group of MAC destination addresses (VLs)

rules.source_quote: Two types of relationship between MAC destination address and ACi should be supported: • One ACi for only one MAC destination address (VLi) • One ACi for a group (several) of MAC destination addresses (VLs): Account Sharing
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can test both mapping types by generating frames with MAC addresses configured for one-to-one or one-to-many relationships.

rules.name: Shared VL must belong to only one account

constraint.value: must be part of one and only one account

rules.source_quote: A shared VL will be part of one and only one account.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with a VL ID configured to belong to multiple accounts and verify policing behavior.

rules.name: Configure BAG values in range 1ms to 128ms
rules.source_quote: The Traffic Policing function of the Switch should at least be configurable for BAG values in the range 1ms to 128 ms.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with BAG values outside the range [1, 128] ms and verify policing behavior.

rules.name: Configure maximum Jitter values in range 0 to 10ms
rules.source_quote: The traffic policing function should at a minimum be configurable for maximum allowed Jitter values in the range 0 to 10 milliseconds.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with jitter values outside the range [0, 10] ms and verify policing behavior.

rules.name: Handle Ethernet frame sizes in range 64 to 1518 octets
rules.source_quote: The traffic policing function should be able to handle at least Ethernet frames sizes (L) in the range [64-1518] octets.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with sizes outside the range [64, 1518] bytes and verify policing behavior (though this may overlap with rule_002 and rule_003).

rules.name: One BAG, jitter, and maximum size value per VL

constraint.value: one BAG value per VL, one jitter value per VL, and one maximum size value per VL

rules.source_quote: There should be one BAG value per VL, one jitter value per VL, and one maximum size value per VL.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with inconsistent BAG, jitter, or size values for the same VL and verify policing behavior.

rules.name: Shared VLs must have identical BAG, Smin, and Smax values

constraint.value: all VLs in a shared account must have the same BAG, Smin, and Smax values

rules.source_quote: When one ACi is used by a group of VL, all the VL of this group should have the same BAG and the same minimum (smin) and maximum (smax) total Ethernet line size values.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with VLs in a shared account having mismatched BAG, Smin, or Smax values and verify policing behavior.

rules.name: Use maximum jitter value of shared VLs for account policing

constraint.value: use the maximum jitter value of all VLs in the group for the account

rules.source_quote: When one ACi is used by a group of VLs, the traffic policing function should use the maximum of the jitter values of all of the VLs in the group as the jitter parameter for the ACi.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with VLs in a shared account having varying jitter values and verify that the maximum jitter is enforced.

rules.name: Policing resolution must be <= 100 microseconds
rules.source_quote: Traffic should be policed with a resolution of less than or equal to 100 μs.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with inter-frame gaps or timing violations smaller than 100 μs and verify policing behavior.

rules.name: Policing rate relative tolerance
rules.source_quote: Traffic should be policed with a relative tolerance on the resolution of ±10-4.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic exceeding the configured policing rate by more than ±0.01% to test if the switch enforces the tolerance limit.

rules.name: Virtual Link frame order preservation

constraint.value: Frames belonging to the same Virtual Link must be forwarded in the same order they were received.

rules.source_quote: The order of input and output frames belonging to a Virtual Link should be maintained by the switch.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames out of order (e.g., swap sequence numbers) and observe if the switch reorders them or discards them.

rules.name: Frame Check Sequence preservation
rules.source_quote: The switch should not modify the Frame Check Sequence of incoming frames. [...] the CRC may not be regenerated within the switch under any circumstance, including at re-transmission.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could modify the FCS field of a frame and verify if the switch forwards it unchanged or discards it.

rules.name: Destination Address-based forwarding

constraint.value: The Destination Address field must be used to determine the output port(s) from the configuration table.

rules.source_quote: For each frame, the content of the Destination Address field should be used to obtain from the configuration table the appropriate port(s) to which the frame has to be forwarded.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a frame with a Destination Address not mapped to any port in the configuration table and observe if the switch discards it or forwards it incorrectly.

rules.name: Frame discard on buffer congestion

constraint.value: Frames must be discarded for an output port if the port cannot accept them due to buffer congestion.

rules.source_quote: If an output port cannot accept a frame due to buffer congestion, this frame should be discarded for this port.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could flood an output port with frames to induce buffer congestion and verify if the switch discards excess frames.

rules.name: Frame discard on link failure

constraint.value: Frames held in buffers for a failed port must be discarded.

rules.source_quote: In the case of a link failure of a port, frames forwarded to and held in buffers of this port should be discarded for this port.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a link failure and verify if the switch discards frames queued for the failed port.

rules.name: Maximum frame delay enforcement

constraint.value: Frames older than the configured 'max delay' parameter must not be transmitted on the output port.

rules.source_quote: An output port should not transmit frames that are older than 'max delay.' The 'max delay' parameter is defined on a per port basis in the configuration table.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could delay frames artificially beyond the 'max delay' value and observe if the switch discards them.

rules.name: Any-to-any port forwarding capability

constraint.value: The switch must be capable of receiving a frame on any port and forwarding it to any combination of ports, including the receiving port.

rules.source_quote: The switch should have the capability to receive a frame on any port and forward it to any combination of ports (including the receiving port).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a frame and verify if the switch can forward it to any port, including the ingress port, as configured.

rules.name: Traffic class prioritization
rules.source_quote: The Switch should have a traffic prioritization mechanism based on MAC destination address with 2 traffic classes: High Priority and Low Priority.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with invalid priority values (e.g., undefined classes) and observe if the switch handles them correctly.

rules.name: High priority frame precedence

constraint.value: High priority frames must be sent before low priority frames on the same output port.

rules.source_quote: For each output port, frames with a priority set to high should be sent prior to the one set to low.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send interleaved high and low priority frames and verify if the switch transmits high priority frames first.

rules.name: Non-preemption of low priority frames

constraint.value: A low priority frame in the process of being transmitted must not be pre-empted by a high priority frame.

rules.source_quote: A low priority frame in the process of being transmitted should not be pre-empted by the arrival of a high priority frame.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a low priority frame followed by a high priority frame during transmission and verify if the switch completes the low priority frame before transmitting the high priority one.

rules.name: Minimum Inter-Frame Gap enforcement

constraint.value: Frames must be sent with a minimum Inter-Frame Gap if other frames are present at the output port.

rules.source_quote: If frames are present at the output port, switch should send them with a minimum Inter Frame Gap.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with an Inter-Frame Gap smaller than the minimum and observe if the switch enforces the gap.

rules.name: Switch End System MAC source address

constraint.value: The switch must use its own MAC unicast address as the MAC Source Address when sending frames.

rules.source_quote: The End System of the switch should use its own MAC unicast address as the MAC Source Address when it sends frames.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a frame from the switch with an incorrect or spoofed MAC Source Address and verify if the switch corrects it or discards the frame.

rules.name: MIB variable update frequency
rules.source_quote: The Fault/Healthy MIB variable should be updated every 100 ms (like the other MIB variables). This will ensure that when the Fault/Healthy indicator is sent it will always get the current status of the Switch.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate SNMP requests at intervals less than 100 ms to verify if the MIB variables reflect stale data or violate the update frequency constraint.

rules.name: Fault/Healthy indicator update frequency
rules.source_quote: The update of the Fault/Healthy indicator output should be performed at least every 100 ms.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a fault condition and verify if the Fault/Healthy indicator is updated within 100 ms. Alternatively, delay updates beyond 100 ms to test enforcement.

rules.name: Fault/Healthy indicator condition

constraint.value: set to 'Fault' when at least one used Ethernet port is in fault

rules.source_quote: The Healthy/Fault indicator should be set to 'Fault' when at least one used Ethernet port is in fault.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a port fault and verify if the Fault/Healthy indicator transitions to 'Fault'. Alternatively, simulate no faults and verify the indicator remains 'Healthy'.

rules.name: Configuration file consistency

constraint.value: All configuration files must be identical for all switches within a network

rules.source_quote: All files have to be identical for all switches within a network.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could load mismatched configuration files across switches and observe if the network behaves inconsistently or raises alarms.

rules.name: Configuration file selection exclusivity

constraint.value: Configuration files are selected in an exclusive mode

rules.source_quote: Depending on the operating mode, the appropriate file is selected in an exclusive mode.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to load multiple configuration files simultaneously and verify if the switch rejects or misbehaves due to non-exclusive selection.

rules.name: Default configuration file usage

constraint.value: Used when the Switch is empty or in Dataloading mode (DL)

rules.source_quote: The Default_Configuration_File, corresponding to the resident configuration, that is used when the Switch is empty (no field loadable software yet loaded) or when the Switch is being dataloaded (in both case, the Switch is in Dataloading mode (DL))
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a dataloading scenario and verify if the switch defaults to the Default_Configuration_File. Alternatively, force the switch out of DL mode and verify it does not use the default file.

rules.name: OPS configuration file usage

constraint.value: Used when the Switch is in Operational mode (OPS)

rules.source_quote: The OPS_Configuration_File, corresponding to the loadable configuration, that is used when the Switch is in Operational mode (OPS)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could force the switch into OPS mode and verify if it uses the OPS_Configuration_File. Alternatively, use the OPS file in DL mode to test enforcement.

rules.name: Switch position pin count (example)

constraint.note: Non-normative example; if implemented, 12 pins must be used

rules.source_quote: In the following paragraphs, it is assumed that the switch position is identified by 12 pins. This should not be considered as normative, but as an example. Nevertheless, if the implementer decides to use 12 pins, the following definitions should be used.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a switch with a non-12 pin configuration and verify if the switch misinterprets its position or fails to extract the correct configuration table.

rules.name: Default configuration table immutability

constraint.value: Can only be changed in shop, associated with a Hardware P/N modification

rules.source_quote: The Default_Configuration_Table is inseparable to the Hardware P/N of the Switch and can only be changed in shop, associated with a Hardware P/N modification.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to modify the Default_Configuration_Table in the field and verify if the switch rejects the change or raises an alarm.

rules.name: Default configuration table residency

constraint.value: Must be resident

rules.source_quote: This table should be resident.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a scenario where the Default_Configuration_Table is missing or corrupted and verify if the switch fails to initialize or defaults to a safe state.

rules.name: Default Physical Port Speed
rules.source_quote: The default port speed should be set to 100 Mbps, without auto negotiation.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic with port speed set to values other than 100 Mbps (e.g., 10 Mbps, 1 Gbps) and observe if the switch rejects or misinterprets the frames.

rules.name: Default Reception VL Identifier Format

constraint.value: VL (0, position), where '0' indicates reception VL and 'position' depends on the switch's location in the aircraft network.

rules.source_quote: Depending of its position in the aircraft network, acquired by pin programming, the Switch subscribes by default to one unique reception VL, further called VL (0, position). '0' indicates that it is a reception VL.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with malformed VL identifiers (e.g., VL (2, position), VL (0, invalid)) and observe if the switch rejects or processes them incorrectly.

rules.name: Default Reception VL Non-Volatile Configuration

constraint.value: Must include VL identifier (MAC destination address), maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax), and Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAG) in non-volatile memory.

rules.source_quote: The reception part of the Default_Configuration_Table of the Switch should contain at least, in nonvolatile memory, the following information (characteristics of the default reception VL): VL identifiers (MAC destination address): VL (0,position), Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax), Bandwidth Allocation Gap.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with missing or corrupted default reception VL configuration parameters and observe if the switch fails to process them.

rules.name: IP Destination Address Validation

constraint.value: The End System Function of the Switch will only take into account the frames whose IP destination field corresponds to its own IP address, deduced from Pin Programming P1 to P12.

rules.source_quote: The End System Function of the Switch will only take into account the frames whose IP destination field corresponds to its own IP address, deduced from Pin Programming P1 to P12 (refer to Section 4.10.2.1).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with incorrect IP destination addresses (e.g., broadcast, multicast, or unrelated unicast addresses) and observe if the switch discards them.

rules.name: Policing Activation on Default Reception VL
rules.source_quote: The policing function of the switch is activated on the default VL, according to the values defined in the configuration file.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames that exceed the configured policing parameters (e.g., BAG or smax) for the default VL and observe if the switch enforces policing (e.g., discards or marks frames).

rules.name: Default Transmission VL Identifier Bit Mapping
rules.source_quote: Where P1 to P12 correspond to the following pin programming values: 1 = GROUND and 0 = OPEN.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with VL identifiers using invalid bit mappings (e.g., values other than 0 or 1 for P1-P12) and observe if the switch rejects or misinterprets them.

rules.name: Default Transmission VL Non-Volatile Configuration

constraint.value: Must include VL identifier (MAC destination address), maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax), and Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAG) in non-volatile memory.

rules.source_quote: The transmission part of the Default_Configuration_Table of the Switch should contain at least, in non-volatile memory, the following information (characteristics of the default transmission VL): VL identifier (MAC destination address): VL (1,position), Bandwidth Allocation GAP, Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with missing or corrupted default transmission VL configuration parameters and observe if the switch fails to transmit them.

rules.name: Source Address Derivation from Pin Programming

constraint.value: When the End System of the Switch sends frames, the IP and MAC source addresses must be derived from Pin Programming P1 to P12.

rules.source_quote: When the End System of the Switch will send frame, the IP and MAC source addresses fields in the AFDX frame will be the own Switch IP and MAC addresses, deduced from Pin Programming P1 to P12 (refer to Section 4.10.2.1).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with incorrect source IP or MAC addresses (e.g., addresses not matching the switch's pin programming) and observe if the switch discards or misroutes them.

rules.name: Uniform OPS Configuration File

constraint.value: The same OPS_Configuration_File (same P/N) must be loaded in all switches of the Avionics Data Communications Network.

rules.source_quote: The same OPS_Configuration_File (same P/N) is loaded in all the Switches of the Avionics Data Communications Network.

rules.name: Switch Position-Based Configuration Access

constraint.value: The switch must only access the dedicated table of the OPS_Configuration_File corresponding to its current position, acquired by pin programming.

rules.source_quote: Depending of its current position, acquired by pin programming, the Switch only has access to the dedicated table of the OPS_Configuration_File.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a switch loading an OPS_Configuration_File table intended for a different position and observe if the switch misconfigures or fails to operate.

rules.name: OPS Configuration File Compliance

constraint.value: The OPS_Configuration_File must be compliant with ARINC 615A and ARINC 665.

rules.source_quote: The OPS_Configuration_File should be a field loadable software file compliant with ARINC 615A and ARINC 665.

rules.name: Received Frame Consistency Check

constraint.value: On the receiving side, the End System function of the switch must check the consistency of the received frame using the EndSystem_Configuration_Table.

rules.source_quote: On the receiving side, check the consistency of the received frame.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with inconsistencies (e.g., mismatched VL identifiers, incorrect frame sizes, or corrupted headers) and observe if the switch discards them.

rules.name: Transmission Flow Control Mechanism

constraint.value: On the transmitting side, the End System function of the switch must construct Ethernet frames and perform the flow control mechanism using the EndSystem_Configuration_Table.

rules.source_quote: On the transmitting side, construct the Ethernet frames and perform the flow control mechanism.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames that violate flow control parameters (e.g., exceeding BAG or smax) and observe if the switch enforces flow control (e.g., delays or discards frames).

rules.name: Filtering and Forwarding Configuration

constraint.value: In Operational mode (OPS), the filtering and forwarding functions must rely on the parameters contained in the Filtering_Policing_and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table corresponding to the switch's current position.

rules.source_quote: In Operational mode (OPS), the filtering and forwarding functions rely on the parameters contained in the Filtering_Policing_and_Forwarding_Configuration_Table, corresponding to the current position of the Switch.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames that violate filtering or forwarding rules (e.g., incorrect VL identifiers, unauthorized MAC addresses) and observe if the switch enforces the rules (e.g., discards or misroutes frames).

rules.name: Virtual Link Output Ports Definition

constraint.value: Must be a non-empty list of valid physical output ports configured for the VL

rules.source_quote: • List of output physical ports
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a frame with a VL configured to output to a non-existent or invalid physical port.

rules.name: MAC Destination Address as VL Identifier

constraint.value: Must uniquely identify the VL (VLi) and comply with MAC address format (48-bit)

rules.source_quote: • MAC destination address (VL identifier VLi)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a frame with an invalid or duplicate MAC destination address for a VL.

rules.name: Bandwidth Allocation Gap (BAG) Constraint
rules.source_quote: • Bandwith Allocation Gap (BAGi)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with a BAG value not in the allowed list (e.g., 3 ms or 200 ms).

rules.name: Maximum Allowed Jitter Constraint
rules.source_quote: • Maximum allowed Jitter
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with jitter exceeding the configured maximum allowed jitter for the VL.

rules.name: Accounting Mode Constraint
rules.source_quote: • ACcount (ACi) [specifying if this account is shared or not]
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with an invalid accounting mode (e.g., neither 'shared' nor 'not_shared').

rules.name: Maximum Allowed Ethernet Frame Size Constraint
rules.source_quote: • Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smax)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames exceeding the configured Smax (e.g., 1519 bytes).

rules.name: VL Prioritization Constraint
rules.source_quote: • Prioritization (high or low)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with an invalid prioritization value (e.g., 'medium').

rules.name: Port State Constraint
rules.source_quote: • Port State (ON/ OFF)
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to send frames through a port configured as 'OFF'.

rules.name: Physical Port Speed Constraint
rules.source_quote: • Speed of the physical port
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate traffic exceeding the configured port speed (e.g., 1000 Mbps on a 100 Mbps port).

rules.name: Output Buffer Size for Low Priority VLs Constraint
rules.source_quote: • Output Buffer Size for Low Priority VLs
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send low-priority frames exceeding the configured output buffer size.

rules.name: Output Buffer Size for High Priority VLs Constraint
rules.source_quote: • Output Buffer Size for High Priority VLs
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send high-priority frames exceeding the configured output buffer size.

rules.name: Switch Operational Mode Transition

constraint.value: Switch must transition to OPS mode after successful initialization and configuration loading.

rules.source_quote: OPS is the operational mode of the Switch. In this mode, the Switch performs operational functions: frame and traffic filtering function, switching function, monitoring function, etc., relying upon the information contained in the loaded configuration tables: OPS_Configuration_File.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a failure in configuration loading to prevent the switch from entering OPS mode.

rules.name: Anomaly Detection in INIT Mode

constraint.value: Anomaly detected during INIT mode must transition the switch to PASSIVE mode.

rules.source_quote: Anomaly detected during the INIT mode will lead to the PASSIVE MODE activation.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate an anomaly (e.g., failed autotest) during INIT mode to verify transition to PASSIVE mode.

rules.name: Catastrophic Failure Mode Transition

constraint.value: Switch must enter QUIET mode in the event of a catastrophic failure.

rules.source_quote: QUIET mode is entered in the event of any sort of catastrophic failure that would cause the functional behavior of the switch to be questionable
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a catastrophic failure (e.g., buffer overflow) to verify transition to QUIET mode.

rules.name: Switch Initialization Time Constraint
rules.source_quote: Therefore, the initialization sequence should be performed in less than a specified initialization time, from power rise to full OPS MODE (all OPS functions are running).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate an initialization sequence exceeding the specified initialization time.

rules.name: Fault Indicator During Initialization

constraint.value: Fault/Healthy indicator must remain in the Fault state during INIT mode.

rules.source_quote: During INIT, the Fault/Healthy indicator should stay in the Fault state.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a premature transition of the Fault/Healthy indicator to Healthy during INIT mode.

rules.name: OPS mode activation conditions
rules.source_quote: After the initialization sequence, the Switch should enter in OPS (operational mode) if the result of compatibility checks is correct and if the shop condition is not active.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a switch with failed compatibility checks or active shop condition to prevent OPS mode activation.

rules.name: OPS mode functions
rules.source_quote: In OPS, the Switch should perform its normal functions (frames filtering and Traffic policing functions, Switching function, End System function) exclusively relying upon the data contained in the activated part of the OPS_Configuration_File.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject frames that test whether the switch enforces filtering, policing, and switching rules in OPS mode.

rules.name: OPS mode ARINC 615A operations
rules.source_quote: In OPS mode, the Switch End System should be able to perform the following ARINC 615A dataloading operations: Information operation, FIND request
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send an ARINC 615A Uploading operation request in OPS mode to test if the switch rejects it.

rules.name: OPS mode Fault/Healthy indicator
rules.source_quote: In OPS mode, the Fault/Healthy indicator should be set in the Healthy state.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could monitor the Fault/Healthy indicator to verify it is set to Healthy in OPS mode.

rules.name: DL mode activation from INIT mode
rules.source_quote: From the INIT MODE, the Switch should enter in DL MODE only if the following conditions are both true: The Switch_Ground_Condition is active, The results of compatibility checks are incorrect or there is no loaded software
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a switch with correct compatibility checks and loaded software to test if DL mode is not entered from INIT.

rules.name: DL mode activation from OPS mode
rules.source_quote: From the OPS MODE, the Switch should enter the DL MODE only if the following conditions are all true: The Switch_Ground_Condition is active, The Switch received an ARINC 615A uploading operation initialization request from the dataloader ([TH_Uploading_Initialization] message) addressed to the own end system of the Switch, The header file has been received and accepted
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send an ARINC 615A uploading initialization request without ground condition or header file to test if DL mode is not entered from OPS.

rules.name: DL mode ARINC 615A session continuity

constraint.value: Transition from OPS mode to DL mode should not disrupt the ARINC 615A session.

rules.source_quote: Transition from OPS mode to DL mode should not disrupt the ARINC 615A session.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could initiate an ARINC 615A session in OPS mode and force a transition to DL mode to verify session continuity.

rules.name: DL mode ARINC 615A operations
rules.source_quote: In DL mode, the Switch should be able to completely perform the following ARINC 615A dataloading operations: Information operation, Uploading operation, FIND request
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send non-ARINC 615A frames in DL mode to test if the switch ignores them.

rules.name: DL mode exclusivity during uploading

constraint.value: During the uploading operation, the Switch is only dedicated to this operation.

rules.source_quote: Uploading is a particular operation that must be preferably exclusive. During the uploading operation, the Switch is only dedicated to this operation.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject non-uploading frames during an uploading operation to test if the switch ignores them.

rules.name: DL mode configuration reliance

constraint.value: Switch should perform its End System function exclusively relying upon the data contained in its resident configuration table: Default_Configuration_Table.

rules.source_quote: In DL Mode, the Switch should perform its End System function exclusively relying upon the data contained in its resident configuration table: Default_Configuration_Table.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could modify the Default_Configuration_Table and observe if the switch behavior changes in DL mode.

rules.name: DL mode Fault/Healthy indicator
rules.source_quote: In DL mode, the Fault/Healthy indicator should be set in the Healthy state.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could monitor the Fault/Healthy indicator to verify it is set to Healthy in DL mode.

rules.name: DL mode exit condition

constraint.value: At the end of the DL mode, the Switch should return to INIT Mode.

rules.source_quote: At the end of the DL mode, the Switch should return to INIT Mode.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate the end of a dataloading operation and verify if the switch returns to INIT mode.

rules.name: Passive mode activation conditions
rules.source_quote: From the INIT mode, the Switch should enter in PASSIVE Mode as soon as one of the following conditions is true: Pin programming parity check fails, Safety Test (if any) result is incorrect
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a switch with correct pin programming or safety test to test if Passive mode is not entered.

rules.name: Passive mode behavior
rules.source_quote: In PASSIVE Mode, the functions of the Switch should be stopped and the switch should keep silent. Nevertheless, the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function should be maintained except if the passive state results from an erroneous parity of the pin programming discretes.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject frames into a switch in Passive mode to test if it remains silent and does not forward frames.

rules.name: Passive mode Fault/Healthy indicator
rules.source_quote: When entering in PASSIVE Mode, the Switch should set the Fault/Healthy indicator in the Fault state.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could monitor the Fault/Healthy indicator to verify it is set to Fault in Passive mode.

rules.name: Passive mode default VLs for management

constraint.value: Default VLs (VL (0, position) and VL (1, position)) are used to communicate with the Network Management Function.

rules.source_quote: The default VLs (called VL (0, position) and VL (1, position) in this document) are used to communicate with the Network Management Function.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send management frames on non-default VLs in Passive mode to test if the switch ignores them.

rules.name: Quiet mode behavior
rules.source_quote: In QUIET mode, the functions of the switch are stopped, the switch does not transmit frames or allow communication with the switch management function (SNMP). The switch software disables all ports when transitioning to QUIET mode.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject frames into a switch in Quiet mode to test if it remains completely silent and does not forward any frames.

rules.name: Quiet mode Fault/Healthy indicator
rules.source_quote: When entering QUIET Mode, the switch sets the Fault/Healthy indicator to the Fault state.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could monitor the Fault/Healthy indicator to verify it is set to Fault in Quiet mode.

rules.name: Quiet mode failure conditions
rules.source_quote: QUIET mode is entered in the event of any sort of catastrophic failure that would cause the functional behavior of the switch to be questionable. Some examples of these types are failures are: Programming pin CRC failure, Heart Beat monitor test failure, Boot Code CRC failure, Processor Instruction test failure, Address/Data Bus monitor failure, RAM memory monitoring failure, Built-In-Self-Test (BIST) failure, Hardware register test failure, Default OPS software CRC check failure, Default Configuration file CRC check failure
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate one of these failures to test if the switch enters Quiet mode.

rules.name: Maximum field loadable software components
rules.source_quote: The Switch should not have more than two field loadable software (OPS_Configuration_File and OPS_Software).

rules.name: Uniformity of field loadable configuration files

constraint.value: OPS_Configuration_File should be the same for all the Switches in the A/C.

rules.source_quote: Those field loadable configuration file should be the same for all the Switches in the A/C.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a switch with a mismatched OPS_Configuration_File and observe if the network rejects or isolates it.

rules.name: Pin programming read condition

constraint.value: Hardware program pins should be read during initialization only if Switch_Ground_Condition is true.

rules.source_quote: Hardware program pins should be read during the initialization (INIT mode) of the SWITCH only if the Switch_Ground_Condition is true and before performing the Safety Test (if any). When the Switch_Ground_Condition is false, hardware program pins should not be read. The Switch should use the last memorized values.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a switch with Switch_Ground_Condition=false and altered pin programming, then observe if the switch uses memorized values or incorrectly reads pins.

rules.name: Pin programming parity check

constraint.value: The 12 program pins (P1 to P12) should be checked by a parity bit.

rules.source_quote: The 12 program pins (P1 to P12) should be checked by a parity bit.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send pin programming with an invalid parity bit and observe if the switch rejects the configuration or fails to initialize.

rules.name: Pin programming non-volatile storage

constraint.value: When program pins are read and parity check passed, program pins should be memorized in non-volatile memory.

rules.source_quote: In order to be used in case of power cut in flight condition, when program pins are read and parity check passed, program pins should be memorized in non-volatile memory of the SWITCH.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a power cycle after valid pin programming and observe if the switch retains the correct configuration.

rules.name: Pin programming value encoding
rules.source_quote: GROUND value of the Pin Programming should be coded as 1. OPEN value of the Pin Programming should be coded as 0.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send pin programming with values outside {0, 1} and observe if the switch rejects or misinterprets the configuration.

rules.name: Maximum supported Virtual Links
rules.source_quote: The filtering, policing, and forwarding function of the switch should be able to process at least 4096 VLs.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a switch configuration with >4096 VLs and observe if the switch rejects the configuration or exhibits degraded performance.

rules.name: Port speed configuration
rules.source_quote: Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a switch port configured to a speed outside {10, 100} Mbps and observe if the port rejects the configuration or fails to operate.

rules.name: Wire speed frame processing

constraint.value: The switch must be able to process (receive, filter, police, relay, transmit) all frames that are incoming at wire speed whatever their size, given a deterministic configuration.

rules.source_quote: Given a deterministic configuration (a deterministic configuration is defined by the absence of any output port saturation) the switch must be able to process (i.e. receive, filter, police, relay, transmit) all frames that are incoming at wire speed whatever their size.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames at wire speed with varying sizes and observe if the switch drops frames or exhibits non-deterministic behavior.

rules.name: Input port fairness

constraint.value: No input port should have priority over another.

rules.source_quote: The previous requirement implicitly imposes a fair processing of the input ports: no input port should have priority over another.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames simultaneously to multiple input ports and observe if one port is consistently prioritized over others.

rules.name: MAC layer wire speed reception

constraint.value: The MAC layer of each switch input port should be able to receive frames at wire speed.

rules.source_quote: The MAC layer of each switch input port should be able to receive frames at wire speed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames at wire speed with minimum interframe gap and observe if the MAC layer drops frames.

rules.name: Wire speed frame filtering

constraint.value: Each switch port should be able to filter frames of any valid size that are arriving at wire speed.

rules.source_quote: Each switch port should be able to filter frames of any valid size that are arriving at wire speed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames at wire speed with varying sizes and observe if the switch fails to filter frames correctly (e.g., forwards invalid frames).

rules.name: Wire speed policing

constraint.value: Each switch port should be able to police the VLs for frames of any valid size that are arriving at wire speed.

rules.source_quote: Each switch port should be able to police the VLs for frames of any valid size that are arriving at wire speed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames at wire speed that exceed VL bandwidth limits and observe if the switch correctly polices (drops) excess frames.

rules.name: Wire speed frame relay

constraint.value: The switch should be able to relay all incoming frames that are not rejected by filtering and policing, at wire speed and whatever their size, given a deterministic configuration.

rules.source_quote: Given a deterministic configuration, the switch should be able to relay all incoming frames that are not rejected by filtering and policing, at wire speed and whatever their size.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames at wire speed and observe if the switch drops frames that should be relayed or exhibits non-deterministic relay behavior.

rules.name: Interframe gap minimum
rules.source_quote: Wire speed is defined as the maximum frame rate achieved when frames are received with a minimum Interframe Gap of 12 octets regardless of frame size.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames with an interframe gap <12 octets and observe if the switch drops frames or exhibits errors.

rules.name: Maximum frame rate at 100 Mbps
rules.source_quote: This corresponds to a maximum frame rate of: 64 bytes (frame) + 12 bytes (IFG) + 7 bytes (Preamble) + 1 byte (SFD) = 84 bytes. When operating at 100 Mbits/s, this corresponds to duration of 6.72 μs per frame (about 148800 frames per second).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames at a rate exceeding 148800 frames/second and observe if the switch drops frames or exhibits errors.

rules.name: Switch technological latency constraint
rules.source_quote: The technological latency of the switch should be less than 100 μs.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with artificially delayed processing in the switch to exceed 100 μs technological latency.

rules.name: Switch output port buffer capacity
rules.source_quote: Each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames (balanced between high and low priority).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic exceeding 512 frames in a burst to test buffer overflow conditions.

rules.name: End System wire-speed throughput capability

constraint.value: End System should handle back-to-back frames (100% wire speed).

rules.source_quote: The maximum throughput ('wire speed') corresponds to back-to-back frames.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate continuous back-to-back frames to test if the End System processes them at wire speed.

rules.name: End System performance calculation formula

constraint.value: Performance = 100 * (1 / (last_frame_latency - technological_latency + 1)) / processing_time

rules.source_quote: Performance = 100 x 1 / (last_frame_latency - technological_latency + 1) / processing_time
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could manipulate last_frame_latency or processing_time to violate the expected performance percentage.

rules.name: Last frame latency measurement points

constraint.value: Latency of the last frame of a 1 ms burst, measured at reception points.

rules.source_quote: The 'last frame latency' corresponds to the latency of the last frame of the 1 ms bursts received, whether this frame corresponds to the B or the A network. The points of measurement are the same as those defined for the latency in reception.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate frames with artificially inflated latency to test if the End System correctly measures last frame latency.

rules.name: End System invariant parameters for performance

value: Size of IP multicast group per VL

rules.source_quote: As a guide, the following invariant parameters should be provided: Volume in transmission and reception given by: Number of ports, Number of VLs, Number of SubVL, Frame size, Size of IP multicast group per VL. Speed in transmission given by: Latency, Frame rate. Speed in reception given by: Latency, Traffic profile.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic violating these parameters (e.g., unsupported frame sizes or frame rates) to test End System compliance.

rules.name: Big Endian Byte Order for Integers

constraint.value: Big Endian (most significant byte first)

rules.source_quote: An aircraft data network for byte order, like the internet standard, specifies that integers are sent with the most significant byte first (i.e., Big Endian style). If one considers the successive bytes in a packet as it travels from one machine to another, a binary integer in that packet has its most significant bytes nearest the beginning of the packet and its least significant byte nearest the end of the packet. Ethernet is defined as being Big Endian.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with Little Endian byte order for integers to violate this rule.

rules.name: Bit Order on Ethernet Medium

constraint.value: Bit 24 is the first bit on the medium, bit 7 is the last bit for a 32-bit integer

rules.source_quote: Bit 24 is the first bit on the medium, bit 7 is the last bit on the medium for this long integer.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with reversed bit order (e.g., LSB first) to violate this rule.

rules.name: Memory to Medium Mapping for Integers

constraint.value: Higher bit numbers and bytes are stored at lower memory addresses and transmitted first on the medium

rules.source_quote: Ethernet is defined as being Big Endian. This means data is represented in memory with higher bit numbers and bytes first (lower address values) followed by the bytes containing lower bit numbers.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with inverted memory-to-medium mapping (e.g., LSB at lower addresses) to violate this rule.

rules.name: Allowed primitive data types for AFDX messages
rules.source_quote: The data element types currently defined for use on aircraft data networks are listed in Table 1-1.0.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames containing data elements not listed in Table 1-1.0 (e.g., custom 16-bit integers or unsupported floating-point formats).

rules.name: Signed_32 Integer bit size and range
rules.source_quote: Signed_32 Integer 32 -231 ... 231 - 1
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with Signed_32 Integer values outside the range [-2³¹, 2³¹ - 1] or with incorrect bit lengths (e.g., 16 or 64 bits).

rules.name: Signed_64 Integer bit size and range
rules.source_quote: Signed_64 Integer 64 -263 … 263 - 1
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with Signed_64 Integer values outside the range [-2⁶³, 2⁶³ - 1] or with incorrect bit lengths (e.g., 32 bits).

rules.name: Float_32 bit size and range
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with Float_32 values outside the specified range or with incorrect bit lengths (e.g., 64 bits).

rules.name: Float_64 bit size and range
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with Float_64 values outside the specified range or with incorrect bit lengths (e.g., 32 bits).

rules.name: Boolean bit size
rules.source_quote: Boolean 32 Not Applicable
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with Boolean values using incorrect bit lengths (e.g., 8 or 16 bits).

rules.name: Opaque data usage constraint

constraint.value: Use of the opaque data type should be avoided as much as possible. AFDX messages should be made up of the defined data primitives whenever possible.

rules.source_quote: Use of the opaque data type, however, should be avoided as much as possible. AFDX messages should be made up of the defined data primitives when ever possible.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames containing excessive or unnecessary opaque data to test network tolerance for non-standard data types.

rules.name: Network-independent bit and byte order

constraint.value: Data elements must have a well-defined bit and byte order enabling applications to send and receive data regardless of the native bit or byte order of host processors.

rules.source_quote: These data types have a well-defined bit and byte order that enables applications to send and receive a data element via the network regardless of the native bit or byte order of the host processors used in the system.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with inconsistent or incorrect bit/byte ordering (e.g., little-endian vs. big-endian mismatches) to test network handling of malformed data.

rules.name: Enumerated type encoding constraint

constraint.value: Enumerated types may be encoded as 32-bit signed integers in transfer syntax, but must map to valid abstract syntax values.

rules.source_quote: The encoding rules might encode this as a 32-bit signed integer, which is one of the allowed transfer syntax data primitives.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with 32-bit signed integers that do not map to any valid enumerated value (e.g., values outside the defined labels in Figure 1-1.1).

rules.name: Signed 32-bit integer representation

constraint.value: two's complement

rules.source_quote: The 32-bit signed integer uses the two’s complement data representation format.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a 32-bit integer with an invalid two's complement representation (e.g., incorrect sign extension or bit pattern).

rules.name: Shorter integer conversion to 32-bit
rules.source_quote: When converting 8 or 16-bit integers into this standard 32-bit two’s complement signed integer, the shorter integer should be sign-extended if it is a signed value, or it should be zero-extended if it is an unsigned value.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a 32-bit integer with incorrect extension (e.g., zero-extending a signed value or sign-extending an unsigned value).

rules.name: Signed 64-bit integer representation

constraint.value: two's complement

rules.source_quote: The 64-bit signed integer uses the two’s complement data representation as shown in Figure 1-2.2.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a 64-bit integer with an invalid two's complement representation.

rules.name: 32-bit floating point formula (normalized)
rules.source_quote: The real number value for normalized numbers is given by the formula: (-1)^S x (1.F) x 2^E.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a 32-bit floating point number with an invalid normalized value (e.g., incorrect sign, exponent, or mantissa).

rules.name: 32-bit floating point formula (de-normalized)
rules.source_quote: The real number value for de-normalized numbers is given by the formula: (-1)^S x (0.F) x 2^E.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a 32-bit floating point number with an invalid de-normalized value (e.g., incorrect sign, exponent, or mantissa).

rules.name: 64-bit floating point formula (normalized)
rules.source_quote: The real number value for normalized numbers is given by the formula: (-1)^S x (1.F) x 2^E.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a 64-bit floating point number with an invalid normalized value (e.g., incorrect sign, exponent, or mantissa).

rules.name: 64-bit floating point formula (de-normalized)
rules.source_quote: The real number value for de-normalized numbers is given by the formula: (-1)^S x (0.F) x 2^E.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a 64-bit floating point number with an invalid de-normalized value (e.g., incorrect sign, exponent, or mantissa).

rules.name: Boolean representation in 32-bit field
rules.source_quote: Booleans are represented by a single bit in a 32-bit field. If just one Boolean is represented by a 32-bit field, bit 0 (least significant bit) is used. If bit 0 is a logical '1' the Boolean is said to be true... If bit 0 is a logical '0' the value of the Boolean is said to be false.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a Boolean in a 32-bit field with an invalid bit position (e.g., using bit 1 instead of bit 0) or invalid values (e.g., 2 for true).

rules.name: No scaling in AFDX messages
rules.source_quote: The integer and floating point data types are never scaled in AFDX messages. The scale factor is always one (1), in contrast to ARINC 429 where parameters quite often have scale factors associated with them other than 1.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a message with a non-unity scale factor (e.g., 2 or 0.5) for an integer or floating point value.

rules.name: Bit-wise packed boolean structure size
rules.source_quote: Booleans may be packed into 32-bit structures (see Figure 1-2.4.2). Each bit will then represent their respective Boolean entities.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a boolean structure with more or fewer than 32 bits (e.g., 31 or 33 bits) to test enforcement of the 32-bit boundary.

rules.name: Boolean bit assignment order

constraint.value: Booleans are assigned starting from the least significant bit (bit 0) toward the most significant bit (bit 31).

rules.source_quote: Booleans are assigned to a structure starting from the least significant bit and filling in toward the most significant bit.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can reverse the bit assignment order (e.g., assign booleans starting from the most significant bit) to test enforcement of the least-to-most significant bit rule.

rules.name: Unused bits in boolean structure
rules.source_quote: Unused bits at the most significant end of the 32-bit structure must be all binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can set unused bits to binary ones (e.g., 0xFFFFFFFF for a structure with only 1 boolean) to test enforcement of the zero-padding rule.

rules.name: String length field size
rules.source_quote: The first 2 bytes of the string structure is a 16-bit unsigned integer, this value is the length of the string (number of characters in the string).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a string with a length field that is not 16 bits (e.g., 8 or 32 bits) to test enforcement of the 16-bit length field rule.

rules.name: String length field value

constraint.value: length_value == number_of_characters_in_data_field

rules.source_quote: The value in the length field defines how many bytes the data field occupies.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can set the length field to a value that does not match the actual number of characters in the data field (e.g., length=5 for a 3-character string) to test enforcement of the length-value consistency rule.

rules.name: String pad field value
rules.source_quote: The pad field places binary zeros in any remaining bytes to fill out the fixed size of the data structure.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can fill the pad field with non-zero values (e.g., 0xFF) to test enforcement of the zero-padding rule.

rules.name: Unused bytes in opaque data structure
rules.source_quote: All unused bytes of an opaque data structure should be filled with binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can fill unused bytes in an opaque data structure with non-zero values (e.g., 0xAA) to test enforcement of the zero-padding rule.

rules.name: Variable length opaque data length field size
rules.source_quote: The variable length opaque data structure is defined as a half word (16 bits) length field followed by a sequence of n bytes.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a variable length opaque data structure with a length field that is not 16 bits (e.g., 8 or 32 bits) to test enforcement of the 16-bit length field rule.

rules.name: Variable length opaque data length field value

constraint.value: length_value == number_of_bytes_in_data_field

rules.source_quote: The length field allows knowing the length of a data element that is stored in the structure even though the data element might not use all of the defined storage area. The length n represents the true length of the data element.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can set the length field to a value that does not match the actual number of bytes in the data field (e.g., length=10 for a 5-byte data field) to test enforcement of the length-value consistency rule.

rules.name: Variable length opaque data pad field value
rules.source_quote: The pad field places binary zeros in any remaining bytes to fill out the fixed size of the data structure.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can fill the pad field with non-zero values (e.g., 0x55) to test enforcement of the zero-padding rule.

rules.name: Implicit message format enforcement

constraint.value: Implicit messages contain only data parameters with no format overhead. The message format is known by the port number it is received on.

rules.source_quote: Implicit messages have no format overhead associated with them. The message contains only the data parameters with no means of identifying how the message content is to be interpreted. The message structure defined in this section is exclusively implicit. An application will know the message format by means of the port number it is received on.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can inject format overhead (e.g., length fields or identifiers) into an implicit message to test whether the network enforces the no-overhead rule for implicit messages.

rules.name: Transport layer port number range
rules.source_quote: Transport layer port assignments are therefore not critical and can be assigned by a system integrator using any values in the range 1 to 65535.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with UDP port numbers outside the range 1-65535 (e.g., 0 or 65536) to test if the network rejects or misroutes them.

rules.name: Reserved word alignment

constraint.value: must be aligned on a 32-bit boundary (address divisible by 4)

rules.source_quote: The Reserved word at the beginning of the message should be aligned on a 32-bit boundary.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where the Reserved word starts at an address not divisible by 4 (e.g., byte 2) to test if the network or application rejects or misaligns the message.

rules.name: Functional Status Set alignment

constraint.value: must be aligned on a 32-bit boundary (address divisible by 4)

rules.source_quote: Functional Status Sets should also be aligned on 32-bit boundaries throughout the message.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where Functional Status Sets start at addresses not divisible by 4 (e.g., byte 6) to test alignment enforcement.

rules.name: Message buffer alignment on receive

constraint.value: must be positioned such that the Reserved word is aligned on a 32-bit boundary

rules.source_quote: When the message is transferred to the application on receive the message should be placed in a buffer in memory that is positioned such that the Reserved word is aligned.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can simulate misaligned message buffers in the receiving application to test if the network or application corrects or rejects the misalignment.

rules.name: Data element alignment

constraint.value: address % element_length == 0

rules.source_quote: A data element is said to be aligned if the address of the element in memory is evenly divisible by the data element length (in bytes). For example, a 4-byte (32-bit) scalar value is aligned if its address is a multiple of 4; an 8-byte scalar value is aligned if its address is a multiple of 8, and so on.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with misaligned data elements (e.g., a 4-byte integer starting at byte 2) to test if the network or application enforces alignment.

rules.name: Variable-length data padding

constraint.value: must be padded to a 2-byte boundary (address divisible by 2)

rules.source_quote: In cases such as this, padding should be used to put the data on a 2-byte boundary (address evenly divisible by 2).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with variable-length data (e.g., strings) starting at odd addresses to test if the network or application enforces 2-byte alignment.

rules.name: Padding for alignment
rules.source_quote: A consequence of using data alignment is an occasional need for padding. Consider the case where a 4-byte scalar is stored at address 0x0008 – 0x000B. If an 8-byte scalar is stored after it is in memory, it will not be stored beginning at address 0x000C as it would not be in proper alignment. It must be stored at address 0x0010 leaving addresses 0x000C thru 0x000F unused, or padding.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with incorrect padding (e.g., 8 bytes of padding where 4 are needed) or missing padding to test if the network or application enforces alignment rules.

rules.name: Double precision float alignment

constraint.value: address divisible by 8 bytes

rules.source_quote: next field (Double precision float – 64 bits) is at an address that is divisible by its length (8 bytes).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where double precision floats are misaligned (e.g., starting at an address not divisible by 8).

rules.name: Functional Status Set size
rules.source_quote: The Functional Status Set (FSS) is a 32-bit field made up of four 8 bit status fields (see Figure 3.4.2).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with FSS fields that are not 32 bits (e.g., 16 bits or 64 bits).

rules.name: Functional Status Set unused bits

constraint.value: must be zeros if no additional Data Sets are used

rules.source_quote: If no other DS are used in a FDS, the remaining 24 bits of the FSS must be zeros.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where unused FSS bits are non-zero.

rules.name: Functional Status Set per Data Set

constraint.value: one status field per Data Set, up to 4 DS per FSS

rules.source_quote: each of the remaining status fields are used to represent health and status for them, up to 4 DS. If more than four DS are desired, a new FSS is added to the FDS followed by one to four DS, and so on.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with more than 4 DS per FSS or missing FSS for additional DS.

rules.name: Functional Data Set payload limit

constraint.value: limited by underlying transport mechanisms (payload size)

rules.source_quote: There is no limit to the number of FDSs (and therefore the number of DSs) that can be placed in a single message except the limitation of the underlying transport mechanisms (payload size).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames exceeding the maximum payload size allowed by the transport layer (e.g., UDP payload limit).

rules.name: Data Set status representation

constraint.value: one status field represents all data primitives in a Data Set

rules.source_quote: all the data primitives in any given data set are represented by one status field. This means that if one data primitive is invalid, the entire Data Set has to be marked as invalid.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where individual data primitives have inconsistent statuses (e.g., some marked invalid while the DS status is valid).

rules.name: Functional Status enumerations
rules.source_quote: The FS is a byte of enumerated type with enumerations as defined in Table 1-2. Condition Definition: ND (no data), NO (normal operation), FT (Functional test), NCD (no computed data).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with invalid FS values (e.g., undefined bytes or reserved values).

rules.name: Functional Status priority

constraint.value: highest priority condition is encoded (Priority 1: ND, Priority 2: NCD, Priority 3: FT, Priority 4: NO)

rules.source_quote: When computing the functional status for a DS it is possible for more than one condition to exist. In that case the condition with the highest priority should be encoded into the status field. Priority 1 is the highest priority, priority 4 is the lowest.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where multiple conditions exist but the lowest priority condition is encoded.

rules.name: No Data condition usage

constraint.value: ND status used if even one data primitive in the DS is not available

rules.source_quote: A ND (no data) status indication should be used if even one data primitive in the DS is not available.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where some data primitives are invalid but the DS status is not ND.

rules.name: Valid Functional Status Values
rules.source_quote: If a receiver reads a functional status value other than 0,3,12, or 48, it will discard the data in the associated DS.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can inject frames with functional_status values outside [0, 3, 12, 48] (e.g., 1, 2, 4, 5, 11, 13, 47, 49) and observe if the receiver discards the associated data set.

rules.name: No Unused Bytes Between Data Primitives

constraint.value: Data primitives must be placed consecutively with no unused bytes between them, except for padding for alignment purposes.

rules.source_quote: Data primitives are placed in the data set one after another with no unused bytes between them except for padding for alignment purposes.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can insert arbitrary unused bytes between data primitives in a data set and observe if the receiver misinterprets or discards the frame.

rules.name: Spare Fields Must Be Zero-Filled

constraint.value: Spare data fields must be filled with binary zeros if unused.

rules.source_quote: Spare data fields should be filled in with binary zeros if unused.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can populate spare fields with non-zero values (e.g., 0xFF, 0xAA, random bytes) and observe if the receiver rejects or misprocesses the frame.

rules.name: Spare Fields Only at End of Data Set

constraint.value: Spare data fields can only be placed at the end of the data set.

rules.source_quote: Spare data fields can only be placed at the end of the DS.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can insert spare fields in the middle of a data set and observe if the receiver misinterprets the data set structure.

rules.name: Reserved Field Must Be Zero-Filled

constraint.value: The 32-bit reserved field must be filled with all binary zeros.

rules.source_quote: The 32-bit reserved field should be filled with all binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can populate the reserved field with non-zero values (e.g., 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x55555555) and observe if the receiver rejects or misprocesses the frame.

rules.name: Global Spare Field Must Be Zero-Filled

constraint.value: The global spare field must be filled with all binary zeros if included in a message.

rules.source_quote: If this field is included in a message, it should be filled with all binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can populate the global spare field with non-zero values and observe if the receiver rejects or misprocesses the frame.

rules.name: No Shifting of Data Set Positions

constraint.value: Modifications to a message must not shift the position of existing data sets within the message.

rules.source_quote: messages should be modified in a manner that does not shift the position of the data sets in the message.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where data sets are reordered or shifted (e.g., inserting bytes before an existing data set) and observe if the receiver misinterprets the frame.

rules.name: Minimum Ethernet payload size
rules.source_quote: The minimum size packet in Ethernet has a payload of 18 bytes. If a message is sent on an AFDX network that is less than 18 bytes long the message will be padded out to 18 bytes before it appears on the medium.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with payloads smaller than 18 bytes (e.g., 1-17 bytes) to test if the network pads them to 18 bytes or rejects them.

rules.name: Parameter removal padding requirement

constraint.value: Replace removed parameters with pad bytes; do not shift remaining message content.

rules.source_quote: When removing a parameter from a data set, replace it with a pad. Do not shift the remainder of the message up and remove the place the parameter was filling.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where parameters are removed without padding or where remaining content is shifted, violating the no-shift rule.

rules.name: Parameter insertion in spare/pad fields

constraint.value: Insert new parameters in spare or pad fields to avoid shifting existing message parameters.

rules.source_quote: Minimize the impact to the message by avoiding a shift of position of the existing message parameters, insert new parameters in spare or pad fields.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where new parameters are inserted in non-spare/pad fields, causing shifts in existing parameters.

rules.name: Global spare usage for new parameters/data sets

constraint.value: Use global spare to add new parameters to the last data set (if covered by existing FS) or to add a new data set (if represented by a different FS).

rules.source_quote: Global spare can be used to add a complete new data set to the end of a message, or be used to add parameters to the last data set defined in the message. The choice of which one to do is driven by the functional status. If the new parameter(s) is covered by the existing FS, put them in the last data set. If the new parameter(s) are represented by a different FS, create a new data set.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames where global spare is misused (e.g., adding parameters to a non-last data set or creating a new data set when existing FS applies).

rules.name: Byte and bit ordering in data primitives

constraint.value: Most significant byte on the left, least significant byte on the right; most significant bit on the left, least significant bit on the right.

rules.source_quote: The boxes that represent a data primitive are intended to represent a group of bytes, the most significant byte on the left, the least significant byte on the right. Also, the bits in the bytes are most significant bit on the left and least significant bit on the right.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with reversed byte or bit order in data primitives to test network validation.

rules.name: Data element alignment via padding

constraint.value: Padding maintains alignment of data elements in the message.

rules.source_quote: The padding in this example maintains the alignment of the data elements.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with misaligned data elements (e.g., unaligned 32-bit integers) to test network handling.

rules.name: TCP PUSH flag aggregation prohibition

constraint.value: MUST NOT aggregate or queue un-pushed data

rules.source_quote: Aggregate or queue un-pushed data 4.2.2.2 X
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate TCP segments with PUSH flags set but aggregate or queue data instead of sending immediately.

rules.name: TCP sender buffering prohibition

constraint.value: MUST NOT buffer data indefinitely if PUSH flag cannot be implemented

rules.source_quote: If cannot, sender buffer indefinitely 4.2.2.2   X  ...then the sending TCP: (1) must not buffer data indefinitely…
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate TCP traffic where data is buffered indefinitely, violating the prohibition.

rules.name: TCP PUSH flag notification to application layer

constraint.value: OPTIONAL (not enforced as MUST or MUST NOT)

rules.source_quote: Notify receiving application of PUSH 4.2.2.2 X  Passing a received PSH flag to the application layer is now OPTIONAL.

rules.name: TCP maximum-sized segment transmission requirement

constraint.value: SHOULD send a maximum-sized segment whenever possible

rules.source_quote: Send maximum size segment when possible 4.2.2.2 X  However, a TCP SHOULD send a maximum-sized segment whenever possible, to improve performance
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate TCP segments smaller than the maximum size when it is possible to send larger segments.

rules.name: Boolean packing direction

constraint.value: Packed Booleans are right-justified and fill bits from right to left, with spare bits on the left

rules.source_quote: Packed Booleans are right justified, they begin filling in bits from right to left with spare on the left.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate Boolean fields packed left-justified or with bits filled from left to right, violating the right-justified requirement.

rules.name: Boolean bit position assignment
rules.source_quote: Position 0 Boolean 0x00C0:0, Position 1 Boolean 0x00C0:1, Position 2 Boolean 0x00C0:2, Position 3 Boolean 0x00C0:3, Spare Spare – 28 0x00C0:4-31
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate Boolean fields with used bits in positions 4-31 or spare bits in positions 0-3.

rules.name: Window size unsigned treatment

constraint.value: MUST be treated as an unsigned number

rules.source_quote: The window size MUST be treated as an unsigned number.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a TCP segment with a negative window size value to test if the receiver treats it as unsigned.

rules.name: Prohibition on shrinking window

constraint.value: SHOULD NOT shrink the window (move right window edge left)

rules.source_quote: A TCP receiver SHOULD NOT shrink the window, i.e., move the right window edge to the left.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a TCP segment that reduces the window size from a previously advertised value.

rules.name: Robustness against window shrinking
