constraint.value: MUST be robust against window shrinking

rules.source_quote: A sending TCP MUST be robust against window shrinking, which may cause 'useable window' to become negative.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate window shrinking to test if the sender handles negative usable window correctly.

rules.name: Receiver window closed indefinitely

constraint.value: MAY keep offered receive window closed indefinitely

rules.source_quote: A TCP MAY keep its offered receive window closed indefinitely.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could test if the sender respects a zero window advertisement for an extended period.

rules.name: Zero window probing support

constraint.value: MUST support probing of zero windows

rules.source_quote: Probing of zero (offered) windows MUST be supported.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could test if the sender initiates zero window probes after a timeout.

rules.name: First zero window probe timing

constraint.value: SHOULD send first zero-window probe after retransmission timeout (RTO)

rules.source_quote: The transmitting host SHOULD send the first zero-window probe when a zero window has existed for the retransmission timeout period.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could test if the sender delays the first probe until after the RTO period.

rules.name: Exponential backoff for zero window probes

constraint.value: SHOULD increase exponentially the interval between successive probes

rules.source_quote: The transmitting host SHOULD increase exponentially the interval between successive probes.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could test if the sender doubles the probe interval after each probe.

rules.name: Connection persistence with zero window

constraint.value: MUST allow the connection to stay open with zero window

rules.source_quote: The sending TCP MUST allow the connection to stay open.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could test if the sender maintains the connection despite prolonged zero window conditions.

rules.name: Urgent pointer location

constraint.value: MUST point to the sequence number of the last octet of urgent data

rules.source_quote: The urgent pointer points to the sequence number of the LAST octet (not LAST+1).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send an urgent pointer that incorrectly points to LAST+1 instead of LAST.

rules.name: Support for arbitrary urgent data length

constraint.value: MUST support a sequence of urgent data of any length

rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST support a sequence of urgent data of any length.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send an unusually long sequence of urgent data to test handling.

rules.name: Asynchronous urgent data notification

constraint.value: MUST inform the application layer asynchronously when urgent data is received

rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST inform the application layer asynchronously whenever it receives an Urgent pointer and there was previously no pending urgent data.

rules.name: Receive TCP option in any segment

constraint.value: MUST be able to receive a TCP option in any segment

rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST be able to receive a TCP option in any segment.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a TCP segment with an option in a non-SYN segment to test handling.

rules.name: Ignore unsupported TCP options

constraint.value: MUST ignore without error any TCP option it does not implement

rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST ignore without error any TCP option it does not implement, assuming that the option has a length field.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a segment with an unsupported TCP option to test if it is ignored.

rules.name: Handle illegal option length

constraint.value: MUST be prepared to handle an illegal option length

rules.source_quote: TCP MUST be prepared to handle an illegal option length.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a TCP option with an illegal length field to test handling.

rules.name: MSS option implementation

constraint.value: MUST implement both sending and receiving the Maximum Segment Size option

rules.source_quote: TCP MUST implement both sending and receiving the Maximum Segment Size option.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could test if the TCP stack correctly processes an MSS option in a SYN segment.

rules.name: MSS option sending condition

constraint.value: SHOULD send MSS option in every SYN segment if receive MSS differs from default 536

rules.source_quote: TCP SHOULD send an MSS (Maximum Segment Size) option in Every SYN segment when its receive MSS differs from the default 536,...
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could test if the sender includes an MSS option when its receive MSS is not 536.

rules.name: Optional MSS option sending

constraint.value: MAY send MSS option always

rules.source_quote: ...and MAY send it always.

rules.name: Default MSS value
rules.source_quote: If an MSS option is not received at connection setup, TCP MUST assume a default send MSS of 536.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could omit the MSS option in a SYN segment to test if the default 536 bytes is assumed.

rules.name: Effective send segment size calculation

constraint.value: min(send_MSS, largest_size_permitted_by_IP_layer)

rules.source_quote: The maximum size of a segment that TCP really sends, the 'effective send MSS,' MUST be the smaller of the send MSS (which reflects the available reassembly buffer size at the remote host) and the largest size permitted by the IP layer.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could test if the sender correctly limits the segment size based on the IP layer's maximum permitted size.

rules.name: TCP checksum generation

constraint.value: MUST generate checksum

rules.source_quote: The sender MUST generate.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a TCP segment with an incorrect checksum to test if it is rejected.

rules.name: TCP checksum validation

constraint.value: MUST check checksum

rules.source_quote: The receiver MUST check it.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a TCP segment with a corrupted checksum to test if it is discarded.

rules.name: Clock-driven ISN selection

constraint.value: MUST use clock-driven selection of initial sequence numbers

rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST use the specified clock-driven selection of initial sequence numbers.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could test if the ISN is predictable or follows a clock-driven pattern.

rules.name: Reject OPEN for broadcast/multicast IP address
rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address (e.g., a broadcast or multicast address).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate an OPEN call with a broadcast or multicast IP address as the remote address and verify the TCP implementation rejects it.

rules.name: Silently discard SYN to broadcast/multicast address
rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a SYN segment to a broadcast or multicast IP address and verify it is silently discarded by the TCP implementation.

rules.name: TIME-WAIT state duration

constraint.value: 2 * MSL

rules.source_quote: When a connection is closed actively, it MUST linger in TIME-WAIT state for a time 2xMSL.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could close a connection and verify the TIME-WAIT state duration is exactly 2 times the Maximum Segment Lifetime (MSL).

rules.name: Retransmission Timeout calculation

constraint.value: Karn's algorithm and Jacobson's algorithm

rules.source_quote: A host TCP MUST implement Karn's algorithm and Jacobson's algorithm for computing the retransmission timeout ("RTO").
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could introduce packet loss and verify the retransmission timeout adapts according to Karn's and Jacobson's algorithms.

rules.name: Exponential backoff for retransmissions

constraint.value: exponential backoff for successive RTO values

rules.source_quote: This implementation also MUST include "exponential backoff" for successive RTO values for the same segment.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could force repeated retransmissions of the same segment and verify the RTO doubles (or follows exponential backoff) each time.

rules.name: Same IP Identification for identical retransmissions
rules.source_quote: If a retransmitted packet is identical to the original packet (which implies not only that the data boundaries have not changed, but also that the window and acknowledgment fields of the header have not changed), then the same IP Identification field MAY be used.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could retransmit an identical packet and verify the IP Identification field remains unchanged.

rules.name: Jacobson Slow Start algorithm

constraint.value: Jacobson Slow Start algorithm

rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST implement this algorithm [Jacobson Slow Start].
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate network congestion and verify the TCP implementation increases its congestion window exponentially during slow start.

rules.name: SYN Retransmission Timeout calculation

constraint.value: same as data segment RTO calculation

rules.source_quote: SYN Retransmission Timeout calculation same as data
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could force SYN retransmissions and verify the RTO calculation matches that of data segments.

rules.name: Send RST on data loss during CLOSE
rules.source_quote: If such a host issues a CLOSE call while received data is still pending in TCP, or if new data is received after CLOSE is called, its TCP SHOULD send a RST to show that data was lost.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could call CLOSE while data is pending or inject data after CLOSE and verify a RST is sent.

rules.name: SYN retransmission algorithm consistency

constraint.value: SYN segments MUST use the same retransmission algorithm as data segments

rules.source_quote: Retransmission of SYN segments SHOULD use the same algorithm as data segments.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate SYN segments with a different retransmission timing or backoff algorithm than data segments.

rules.name: Initial RTT estimation
rules.source_quote: RTT = 0 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could initialize RTT to a non-zero value (e.g., 1 second) for a new connection.

rules.name: Initial RTO value
rules.source_quote: RTO = 3 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could initialize RTO to a value other than 3 seconds (e.g., 1 second or 10 seconds).

rules.name: RTO lower bound

constraint.value: measured in fractions of a second

rules.source_quote: The lower bound SHOULD be measured in fractions of a second
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could set the RTO lower bound to a value >= 1 second (e.g., 1 second).

rules.name: RTO upper bound
rules.source_quote: the upper bound should be 2*MSL, i.e., 240 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could set the RTO upper bound to a value other than 240 seconds (e.g., 120 seconds or 300 seconds).

rules.name: Out-of-order segment queuing
rules.source_quote: A TCP SHOULD be capable of queueing out-of-order TCP segments.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send out-of-order segments and verify if the receiver drops them instead of queuing.

rules.name: ACK aggregation

constraint.value: MUST process all queued data before sending ACK

rules.source_quote: the processing of received segments MUST be implemented to aggregate ACK segments whenever possible.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send rapid segments and verify if the receiver sends separate ACKs for each instead of aggregating.

rules.name: ACK for out-of-order segment
rules.source_quote: A TCP MAY send an ACK segment acknowledging RCV.NXT when a valid segment arrives that is in the window but not at the left window edge.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send an out-of-order segment and verify if the receiver sends an ACK for RCV.NXT.

rules.name: Delayed ACK implementation
rules.source_quote: A TCP SHOULD implement a delayed ACK
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could verify if the receiver sends immediate ACKs instead of delaying them.

rules.name: Maximum ACK delay
rules.source_quote: The delay MUST be less than 0.5 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could delay ACKs for >= 0.5 seconds (e.g., 0.6 seconds).

rules.name: ACK frequency for full-size segments

constraint.value: ACK for at least every second full-size segment

rules.source_quote: In a stream of full-sized segments there SHOULD be an ACK for at least every second segment.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send 3+ full-size segments without an ACK for the second segment.

rules.name: Receiver SWS avoidance
rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST include a SWS avoidance algorithm in the receiver.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send segments that trigger SWS and verify if the receiver avoids it (e.g., by adjusting window size).

rules.name: TTL configuration requirement
rules.source_quote: The TTL value used to send TCP segments MUST be configurable.

rules.name: TTL default value in AFDX
rules.source_quote: default value is 1
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could set TTL to a value other than 1 (e.g., 64 or 255).

rules.name: Sender SWS avoidance
rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST include a SWS avoidance algorithm in the sender.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send segments that trigger SWS and verify if the sender avoids it (e.g., by delaying small segments).

rules.name: Nagle algorithm implementation
rules.source_quote: A TCP SHOULD implement the Nagle Algorithm [TCP:9] to coalesce short segments.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send rapid small segments and verify if they are coalesced into larger segments.

rules.name: Nagle algorithm disable capability
rules.source_quote: There MUST be a way for an application to disable the Nagle algorithm on an individual connection.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could verify if the Nagle algorithm remains enabled even when explicitly disabled by the application.

rules.name: Negative advice on R1 retransmissions

constraint.value: MUST pass negative advice to IP layer when retransmissions >= R1

rules.source_quote: When the number of transmissions of the same segment reaches or exceeds threshold R1, pass negative advice to the IP layer, to trigger dead-gateway diagnosis.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could trigger R1 retransmissions and verify if negative advice is not passed to the IP layer.

rules.name: Close connection on R2 retransmissions

constraint.value: MUST close connection when retransmissions >= R2

rules.source_quote: When the number of transmissions of the same segment reaches a threshold R2 greater than R1, close the connection.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could trigger R2 retransmissions and verify if the connection is not closed.

rules.name: Application control of R2
rules.source_quote: An application MUST be able to set the value for R2 for a particular connection.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could verify if the application is unable to set R2 (e.g., R2 is hardcoded).

rules.name: Application notification of retransmissions

constraint.value: SHOULD inform application when R1 <= retransmissions < R2

rules.source_quote: TCP SHOULD inform the application of the delivery Problem (unless such information has been disabled by the application; see Section 4.2.4.1), when R1 is reached and before R2.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could trigger retransmissions between R1 and R2 and verify if the application is not notified.

rules.name: Recommended R1 value

constraint.value: at least 3 retransmissions at current RTO

rules.source_quote: The value of R1 SHOULD correspond to at least 3 retransmissions, at the current RTO.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could set R1 to a value corresponding to fewer than 3 retransmissions (e.g., 1 or 2).

rules.name: Recommended R2 value
rules.source_quote: The value of R2 SHOULD correspond to at least 100 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could set R2 to a value less than 100 seconds (e.g., 50 seconds).

rules.name: SYN retransmission handling

constraint.value: MUST handle SYN retransmissions like data retransmissions

rules.source_quote: SYN Retransmissions MUST be handled in the general way just described for data retransmissions, including notification of the application layer.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could trigger SYN retransmissions and verify if they are handled differently from data retransmissions.

rules.name: R2 for SYN segments
rules.source_quote: R2 for a SYN segment MUST be set large enough to provide retransmission of the segment for at least 3 minutes.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could set R2 for SYN segments to a value less than 180 seconds (e.g., 60 seconds).

rules.name: Keep-alive packets in AFDX
rules.source_quote: keep alive packets are useless.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send keep-alive packets and verify if they are processed or ignored.

rules.name: Keep-alive implementation option
rules.source_quote: Implementors MAY include 'Keep live' in their TCP implementation.

rules.name: Keep-alive default state
rules.source_quote: Default is 'off'
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could enable keep-alive by default and verify if it remains off.

rules.name: Keep-alive default state
rules.source_quote: If keep-alives are included, they MUST default to off.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate TCP traffic with keep-alive enabled by default to violate this rule.

rules.name: Keep-alive transmission condition

constraint.value: Only send if no data or acknowledgement packets have been received for the connection within an interval.

rules.source_quote: Keep-alive packets MUST only be sent when no data or Acknowledgement packets have been received for the connection within an interval.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send keep-alive packets even when data or acknowledgements are actively being exchanged.

rules.name: Keep-alive interval configurability
rules.source_quote: This interval MUST be configurable.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate TCP traffic with a non-configurable keep-alive interval.

rules.name: Keep-alive default interval
rules.source_quote: Default is at least 2 hours
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could set the keep-alive interval to less than 2 hours by default.

rules.name: Keep-alive failure interpretation

constraint.value: MUST NOT interpret failure to respond to any specific probe as a dead connection.

rules.source_quote: If a keep-alive mechanism is implemented it MUST NOT interpret failure to respond to any specific probe as a dead connection.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a TCP implementation that closes connections after a single keep-alive probe failure.

rules.name: Ignore unknown IP options

constraint.value: MUST ignore options that it does not understand.

rules.source_quote: When received options are passed up to TCP from the IP layer, TCP MUST ignore options that it does not understand.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate TCP traffic with malformed or unknown IP options and check if they are incorrectly processed.

rules.name: Time Stamp support
rules.source_quote: A TCP MAY support the Time Stamp.

rules.name: Record Route support
rules.source_quote: A TCP MAY support the Record Route options.

rules.name: Application-specified source route

constraint.value: MUST be able to specify a source route when it actively opens a TCP connection.

rules.source_quote: An application MUST be able to specify a source route when it actively opens a TCP connection.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to open a TCP connection without allowing the application to specify a source route.

rules.name: Override source route precedence

constraint.value: MUST take precedence over a source route received in a datagram.

rules.source_quote: This MUST take precedence over a source route received in a datagram.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic where a received source route overrides an application-specified source route.

rules.name: Return route construction from source route

constraint.value: MUST save the return route and use it for all segments sent on this connection when a packet arrives with a completed IP Source Route option.

rules.source_quote: When a TCP connection is OPENed passively and a packet arrives with a completed IP Source Route option (containing a return route), TCP MUST save the return route and use it for all segments sent on this connection.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic where the return route is not saved or used for subsequent segments.

rules.name: Later source route override

constraint.value: SHOULD override the earlier one if a different source route arrives in a later segment.

rules.source_quote: If a different source route arrives in a later segment, the later definition SHOULD override the earlier one.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic where an earlier source route is retained despite a later conflicting source route.

rules.name: ICMP message restriction
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate ICMP messages other than 'echo request' or 'echo reply' to test enforcement.

rules.name: ICMP Destination Unreachable soft error reaction

constraint.value: MUST NOT abort the connection for codes 0, 1, 5.

rules.source_quote: Since these Unreachable messages indicate soft error conditions, TCP MUST NOT abort the connection.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a TCP implementation that aborts connections on receiving ICMP Destination Unreachable codes 0, 1, or 5.

rules.name: ICMP Destination Unreachable hard error reaction

constraint.value: SHOULD abort the connection for codes 2, 4.

rules.source_quote: Destination Unreachable -- codes 2-4 These are hard error conditions, so TCP SHOULD abort the connection.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a TCP implementation that does not abort connections on receiving ICMP Destination Unreachable codes 2 or 4.

rules.name: ICMP Source Quench reaction

constraint.value: MUST react by slowing transmission on the connection, triggering a 'slow start'.

rules.source_quote: TCP MUST react to a Source Quench by slowing transmission on the connection. The RECOMMENDED procedure is for a Source Quench to trigger a "slow start," as if a retransmission timeout had occurred.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate traffic where a TCP implementation does not slow transmission after receiving an ICMP Source Quench.

rules.name: ICMP Time Exceeded reaction

constraint.value: MUST tell the application and not abort the connection.

rules.source_quote: This should be handled the same way as Destination Unreachable codes 0, 1, 5.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a TCP implementation that aborts connections on receiving ICMP Time Exceeded messages.

rules.name: ICMP Parameter Problem reaction

constraint.value: MUST tell the application and not abort the connection.

rules.source_quote: This should be handled the same way as Destination Unreachable codes 0, 1, 5.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a TCP implementation that aborts connections on receiving ICMP Parameter Problem messages.

rules.name: Reject OPEN call to invalid IP address

constraint.value: MUST reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address.

rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to open a TCP connection to an invalid IP address and check if the call is incorrectly accepted.

rules.name: Reject SYN from invalid IP address

constraint.value: MUST ignore an incoming SYN with an invalid source address.

rules.source_quote: An incoming SYN with an invalid source address must be ignored either by TCP or by the IP layer.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate SYN packets with invalid source IP addresses and check if they are incorrectly processed.

rules.name: Discard SYN to broadcast/multicast address

constraint.value: MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.

rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate SYN segments addressed to broadcast or multicast addresses and check if they are incorrectly processed.

rules.name: TOS field handling in AFDX

constraint.value: TOS is not used by AFDX and must not influence network behavior

rules.source_quote: TOS is not used by AFDX
rules.source_section: Attachment 2, Page 111, Table TCP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can set arbitrary TOS values in TCP segments and verify that AFDX switches/end systems ignore them (e.g., no QoS differentiation based on TOS).

rules.name: TOS pass-through requirement

constraint.value: TCP SHOULD pass the current TOS value unchanged to the IP layer

rules.source_quote: TCP SHOULD pass the current TOS value without change to the IP layer, when it sends segments on the connection.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2, Page 111, Table TCP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can verify that TOS values set in TCP segments are preserved in the IP header of transmitted frames, even if AFDX ignores them.

rules.name: ICMP Port Unreachable suppression
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP 'echo request' and 'echo reply' are allowed. If a datagram arrives addressed to a UDP port for which there is no pending LISTEN call, UDP SHOULD send an ICMP Port Unreachable message.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2, Page 112, Table UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send UDP datagrams to closed ports and verify that no ICMP Port Unreachable messages are generated by AFDX end systems.

rules.name: IP options handling in AFDX

constraint.value: IP options are not used in AFDX and must be ignored or discarded

rules.source_quote: IP options are not used in AFDX
rules.source_section: Attachment 2, Page 112, Table UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can include IP options in UDP datagrams and verify that AFDX switches/end systems discard them or pass them transparently without processing.

rules.name: UDP checksum handling in AFDX
rules.source_quote: Checksum is not used in AFDX
rules.source_section: Attachment 2, Page 112, Table UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send UDP datagrams with invalid checksums and verify that AFDX end systems do not discard them based on checksum validation.

rules.name: Silent discard of UDP datagrams with bad checksums

constraint.value: UDP MUST silently discard datagrams with non-zero and invalid checksums

rules.source_quote: If a UDP datagram is received with a checksum that is non-zero and invalid, UDP MUST silently discard the datagram.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2, Page 113, Table UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send UDP datagrams with non-zero invalid checksums and verify that AFDX end systems discard them without generating errors (though AFDX may ignore checksums entirely).

rules.name: UDP checksum generation default

constraint.value: UDP checksum generation MUST default to enabled

rules.source_quote: it MUST default to checksumming on.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2, Page 113, Table UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can verify that UDP datagrams are transmitted with checksums enabled by default, even if AFDX ignores them.

rules.name: Invalid IP source address discard

constraint.value: UDP datagrams with invalid IP source addresses (e.g., broadcast/multicast) MUST be discarded

rules.source_quote: A UDP datagram received with an invalid IP source address (e.g., a broadcast or multicast address) must be discarded by UDP or by the IP layer.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2, Page 113, Table UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send UDP datagrams with broadcast/multicast source addresses and verify that AFDX end systems discard them.

rules.name: Valid IP source address requirement for transmission

constraint.value: UDP datagrams MUST use one of the host's IP addresses as the source address

rules.source_quote: When a host sends a UDP datagram, the source address MUST be (one of) the IP address(es) of the host.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2, Page 113, Table UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send UDP datagrams with spoofed source IP addresses and verify that AFDX end systems reject or discard them.

rules.name: ICMP message restrictions in AFDX
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP 'echo request' and 'echo reply' are allowed.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2, Page 112, Table UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send ICMP messages of types other than 'echo request' or 'echo reply' and verify that AFDX end systems discard them.

rules.name: Silently discard non-IPv4 datagrams
rules.source_quote: A datagram whose version number is not 4 MUST be silently discarded.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a datagram with IP version set to a value other than 4 (e.g., 5 or 6) and verify it is discarded by the receiving End System.

rules.name: Verify IP header checksum and discard if invalid

constraint.value: MUST verify checksum and silently discard if invalid

rules.source_quote: A host MUST verify the IP header checksum on every received datagram and silently discard every datagram that has a bad checksum.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a datagram with an incorrect IP header checksum and verify it is discarded by the receiving End System.

rules.name: Support subnet addressing
rules.source_quote: A host MUST support the subnet extensions to IP [IP:3].
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate traffic with subnet-specific addressing and verify the End System processes it correctly. Violation: send traffic with malformed subnet addressing.

rules.name: Source address must be host's own IP address

constraint.value: MUST be one of the host's own IP addresses (not broadcast or multicast)

rules.source_quote: When a host sends any datagram, the IP source address MUST be one of its own IP addresses (but not a broadcast or multicast address).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a datagram with a source IP address that does not belong to the sending End System and verify it is discarded or rejected.

rules.name: Silently discard datagram with incorrect destination address

constraint.value: MUST silently discard if not destined for the host

rules.source_quote: A host MUST silently discard an incoming datagram that is not destined for the host.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a datagram with a destination IP address that does not match the receiving End System's IP address and verify it is discarded.

rules.name: Silently discard datagram with invalid source address

constraint.value: MUST silently discard if source address is invalid

rules.source_quote: A host MUST silently discard an incoming datagram containing an IP source address that is invalid by the rules of this section.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a datagram with an invalid source IP address (e.g., loopback, multicast, or broadcast) and verify it is discarded.

rules.name: Support IP reassembly
rules.source_quote: The Internet model requires that every host support Reassembly.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate fragmented IP datagrams and verify the receiving End System reassembles them correctly. Violation: send malformed fragments.

rules.name: Retain same Identification field for identical datagrams

constraint.value: MAY optionally retain the same Identification field for identical datagrams

rules.source_quote: When sending an identical copy of an earlier datagram, a host MAY optionally retain the same Identification field in the copy.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate identical datagrams with different Identification fields and observe if the End System handles them correctly. Violation: enforce strict retention when not required.

rules.name: Allow transport layer to set TOS field

constraint.value: MUST provide a means for the transport layer to set the TOS field; default is all zero bits

rules.source_quote: The IP layer MUST provide a means for the transport layer to set the TOS field of every datagram that is sent; the default is all zero bits.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate datagrams with non-zero TOS values and verify the End System processes them. Violation: ignore TOS settings from the transport layer.

rules.name: Pass received TOS to transport layer

constraint.value: SHOULD pass received TOS values up to the transport layer

rules.source_quote: The IP layer SHOULD pass received TOS values up to the transport layer.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate datagrams with non-zero TOS values and verify the transport layer receives them. Violation: drop TOS values during processing.

rules.name: Do not implement RFC-795 TOS mappings

constraint.value: SHOULD NOT implement RFC-795 link-layer mappings for TOS

rules.source_quote: The particular link-layer mappings of TOS contained in RFC-795 SHOULD NOT be implemented.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can verify that the End System does not apply RFC-795 TOS mappings. Violation: apply RFC-795 mappings incorrectly.

rules.name: Do not send datagram with TTL of zero
rules.source_quote: A host MUST NOT send a datagram with a Time-to-Live (TTL) value of zero.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a datagram with TTL set to 0 and verify it is not transmitted by the End System.

rules.name: Discard received packets with TTL less than 2
rules.source_quote: Discard received packets with TTL < 2
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a datagram with TTL set to 1 and verify it is discarded by the receiving End System.

rules.name: Provide full IP/transport interface services

constraint.value: MUST provide full services of the IP/transport interface (GET_SRCADDR, GET_MAXSIZES, ADVISE_DELIVPROB, RECV_ICMP)

rules.source_quote: The application interface to UDP MUST provide the full services of the IP/transport interface described in Section 3.4 of this document. Thus, an application using UDP needs the functions of the GET_SRCADDR(), GET_MAXSIZES(), ADVISE_DELIVPROB(), and RECV_ICMP() calls described in Section 3.4.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can attempt to use these interface functions and verify they are available. Violation: omit or disable one or more of these functions.

rules.name: Allow application to set TTL, TOS, and IP options

constraint.value: MUST allow application to set TTL, TOS, and IP options for sending a UDP datagram

rules.source_quote: An application-layer program MUST be able to set the TTL and TOS values as well as IP options for sending a UDP datagram, and these values must be passed transparently to the IP layer.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate UDP datagrams with non-default TTL, TOS, or IP options and verify they are transmitted correctly. Violation: ignore application settings for these fields.

rules.name: Pass received TOS to application layer

constraint.value: MAY pass the received TOS up to the application layer

rules.source_quote: UDP MAY pass the received TOS up to the application layer.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate UDP datagrams with non-zero TOS values and verify the application layer receives them. Violation: drop TOS values before reaching the application layer.

rules.name: Disable gateway function by default
rules.source_quote: this switch MUST default to the non-gateway mode.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can verify that the End System does not forward datagrams by default. Violation: enable gateway mode by default.

rules.name: Do not autoconfigure gateway mode based on interfaces

constraint.value: MUST NOT automatically move into gateway mode if the host has more than one interface

rules.source_quote: The host software MUST NOT automatically move into gateway mode if the host has more than one interface.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can simulate a host with multiple interfaces and verify it does not enter gateway mode automatically. Violation: enable gateway mode based on interface count.

rules.name: Log discarded datagrams

constraint.value: SHOULD provide capability to log discarded datagrams, including contents

rules.source_quote: However, for diagnosis of problems a host SHOULD provide the capability of logging the error (see Section 1.2.3), including the contents of the silently-discarded datagram…
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate invalid datagrams and verify they are logged when discarded. Violation: discard datagrams without logging.

rules.name: Record discarded datagrams in counter

constraint.value: SHOULD record discarded datagrams in a statistics counter

rules.source_quote: …and SHOULD record the event in a statistics counter.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate invalid datagrams and verify the discard count increments. Violation: discard datagrams without updating the counter.

rules.name: TTL minimum acceptance

constraint.value: MUST NOT discard datagram with TTL < 2

rules.source_quote: A host MUST NOT discard a datagram just because it was received with TTL less than 2.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate an IP datagram with TTL=1 and send it to an AFDX End System to verify it is not discarded.

rules.name: Transport layer IP options specification

constraint.value: MUST allow transport layer to specify IP options for transmitted datagrams

rules.source_quote: There MUST be a means for the transport layer to specify IP options to be included in transmitted IP datagrams.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate datagrams with various IP options and verify the End System allows their inclusion.

rules.name: Stream Identifier option handling

constraint.value: MUST silently ignore Stream Identifier option if received; SHOULD NOT send it

rules.source_quote: This option is obsolete; it SHOULD NOT be sent… and it MUST be silently ignored if received.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a datagram with the Stream Identifier option and verify it is silently ignored.

rules.name: Source Route option support

constraint.value: MUST support originating a source route and acting as final destination

rules.source_quote: A host MUST support originating a source route and MUST be able to act as the final destination of a source route.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could generate datagrams with Source Route options and verify the End System processes them correctly.

rules.name: Non-redundant return route construction

constraint.value: MUST build correct (non-redundant) return route even if recorded route includes source host

rules.source_quote: When a Return source route is built, it MUST be correctly formed even if the recorded route included the source host.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a Source Route option with redundant entries and verify the return route is correctly formed.

rules.name: Silently discard unknown ICMP messages

constraint.value: MUST silently discard ICMP messages of unknown type

rules.source_quote: If an ICMP message of unknown type is received, it MUST be silently discarded.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send ICMP messages with unknown types and verify they are silently discarded.

rules.name: ICMP error message content

constraint.value: MUST include Internet header and at least first 8 data octets of triggering datagram; more than 8 octets MAY be sent

rules.source_quote: Every ICMP error message includes the Internet header and at least the first 8 data octets of the datagram that triggered the error; more than 8 octets MAY be sent.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could trigger ICMP errors and verify the response includes at least 8 octets of the original datagram.

rules.name: ICMP error message TOS
rules.source_quote: An ICMP error message SHOULD be sent with normal (i.e., zero) TOS bits.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send ICMP error messages with non-zero TOS bits and verify they are corrected or rejected.

rules.name: Prohibition of ICMP error messages in AFDX
rules.source_quote: No ICMP errors
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP error messages (e.g., Destination Unreachable, Source Quench, Time Exceeded, Parameter Problem) and send them to an AFDX End System to verify they are discarded or not processed.

rules.name: Rejection of invalid source IP addresses
rules.source_quote: a datagram whose source address does not define a single host -- e.g., a zero address, a loopback address, a broadcast address, a multicast address, or a Class address.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate IP datagrams with invalid source addresses (e.g., 0.0.0.0, 127.0.0.1, 255.255.255.255, multicast addresses) and verify they are discarded by the AFDX End System.

rules.name: Prohibition of ICMP Redirect messages from End Systems
rules.source_quote: A host SHOULD NOT send an ICMP Redirect message; Redirects are to be sent only by gateways.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Redirect messages from an AFDX End System and verify they are discarded or not processed by the receiving End System.

rules.name: Validation of ICMP Redirect message gateway address

constraint.value: The new gateway address must be on the same connected (sub-)net through which the Redirect arrived, and the source of the Redirect must be the current first-hop gateway for the specified destination.

rules.source_quote: A Redirect message SHOULD be silently discarded if the new gateway address it specifies is not on the same connected (sub-) net through which the Redirect arrived, or if the source of the Redirect is not the current first-hop gateway for the specified destination.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Redirect messages with invalid gateway addresses (e.g., off-subnet or from a non-first-hop gateway) and verify they are discarded by the receiving End System.

rules.name: Restriction to ICMP Echo Request and Echo Reply messages
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP 'echo request' and 'echo reply' are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP messages other than Echo Request or Echo Reply (e.g., Source Quench, Time Exceeded, Parameter Problem) and verify they are discarded by the AFDX End System.

rules.name: Conditional transmission of ICMP Source Quench messages

constraint.value: A host MAY send a Source Quench message if it is approaching or has reached the point of discarding datagrams due to buffer or resource shortages.

rules.source_quote: A host MAY send a Source Quench message if it is approaching, or has reached, the point at which it is forced to discard incoming datagrams due to a shortage of reassembly buffers or other resources.

rules.name: Prohibition of ICMP Source Quench processing in AFDX
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP 'echo request' and 'echo reply' are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Source Quench messages and verify they are discarded or not processed by the AFDX End System.

rules.name: Prohibition of ICMP Time Exceeded processing in AFDX
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP 'echo request' and 'echo reply' are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Time Exceeded messages and verify they are discarded or not processed by the AFDX End System.

rules.name: Prohibition of ICMP Parameter Problem processing in AFDX
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP 'echo request' and 'echo reply' are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Parameter Problem messages and verify they are discarded or not processed by the AFDX End System.

rules.name: Prohibition of ICMP Destination Unreachable processing in AFDX
rules.source_quote: No ICMP errors
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Destination Unreachable messages (codes 0, 1, 2, 3, 5) and verify they are discarded or not processed by the AFDX End System.

rules.name: Interpretation of transient ICMP Destination Unreachable codes
rules.source_quote: A Destination Unreachable message that is received with code 0 (Net), 1 (Host), or 5 (Bad Source Route) may result from a routing transient and MUST therefore be interpreted as only a hint.

rules.name: Restrict ICMP message types to Echo Request and Echo Reply
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP messages with types other than 'echo_request' or 'echo_reply' (e.g., 'timestamp_request', 'information_request') and verify if they are discarded or rejected by the network.

rules.name: Mandatory ICMP Echo server function
rules.source_quote: Every host MUST implement an ICMP Echo server function that receives Echo Requests and sends corresponding Echo Replies.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send ICMP Echo Requests to an End System and verify if it responds with an Echo Reply. Absence of a reply violates this rule.

rules.name: Silently discard Echo Request to broadcast or multicast address

constraint.value: MAY silently discard

rules.source_quote: An ICMP Echo Request destined to an IP broadcast or IP multicast address MAY be silently discarded.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send ICMP Echo Requests to broadcast or multicast addresses and verify if they are silently discarded (no reply or error message).

rules.name: Echo Reply source address must match Echo Request destination address

constraint.value: MUST be the same as the specific-destination address of the corresponding ICMP Echo Request

rules.source_quote: The IP source address in an ICMP Echo Reply MUST be the same as the specific-destination address (defined in Section 3.2.1.3) of the corresponding ICMP Echo Request message.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Echo Request with a specific destination address and verify if the Echo Reply's source address matches it. Mismatch violates this rule.

rules.name: Echo Reply must include all data from Echo Request

constraint.value: MUST entirely include the data received in the ICMP Echo Request

rules.source_quote: Data received in an ICMP Echo Request MUST be entirely included in the resulting Echo Reply.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Echo Request with specific data payload and verify if the Echo Reply contains the exact same payload. Truncation or modification violates this rule.

rules.name: Pass Echo Reply to ICMP user interface

constraint.value: MUST be passed to the ICMP user interface unless the Echo Request originated in the IP layer

rules.source_quote: Echo Reply messages MUST be passed to the ICMP user interface, unless the corresponding Echo Request originated in the IP layer.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Echo Request from an application layer and verify if the Echo Reply is delivered to the application. Failure to deliver violates this rule.

rules.name: Reflect Record Route and Time Stamp options in Echo Reply

constraint.value: SHOULD update and include Record Route and/or Time Stamp options without truncation

rules.source_quote: If a Record Route and/or Time Stamp option is received in an ICMP Echo Request, this option (these options) SHOULD be updated to include the current host and included in the IP header of the Echo Reply message, without "truncation".
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Echo Request with Record Route or Time Stamp options and verify if the Echo Reply includes the updated options without truncation. Missing or truncated options violate this rule.

rules.name: Reverse and reflect Source Route option in Echo Reply

constraint.value: MUST reverse the return route and use it as a Source Route option for the Echo Reply

rules.source_quote: If a Source Route option is received in an ICMP Echo Request, the return route MUST be reversed and used as a Source Route option for the Echo Reply message.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Echo Request with a Source Route option and verify if the Echo Reply uses the reversed route. Incorrect or missing reversed route violates this rule.

rules.name: Prohibit ICMP Information Request or Reply messages
rules.source_quote: A host SHOULD NOT implement these messages.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Information Request or Reply messages and verify if they are discarded or rejected by the network.

rules.name: Optional implementation of ICMP Timestamp and Timestamp Reply

constraint.value: MAY implement

rules.source_quote: A host MAY implement Timestamp and Timestamp Reply.

rules.name: Minimize delay variability for Timestamp messages

constraint.value: SHOULD be designed for minimum variability in delay

rules.source_quote: If this function is implemented, it SHOULD be designed for minimum variability in delay.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send multiple ICMP Timestamp Requests and measure the variability in delay for Timestamp Replies. High variability may indicate a violation of this recommendation.

rules.name: Silently discard Timestamp Request to broadcast or multicast address

constraint.value: MAY silently discard

rules.source_quote: An ICMP Timestamp Request message to an IP broadcast or IP multicast address MAY be silently discarded.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send ICMP Timestamp Requests to broadcast or multicast addresses and verify if they are silently discarded (no reply or error message).

rules.name: Timestamp Reply source address must match Timestamp Request destination address

constraint.value: MUST be the same as the specific-destination address of the corresponding Timestamp Request

rules.source_quote: The IP source address in an ICMP Timestamp Reply MUST be the same as the specific-destination address of the corresponding Timestamp Request message.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Timestamp Request with a specific destination address and verify if the Timestamp Reply's source address matches it. Mismatch violates this rule.

rules.name: Reverse and reflect Source Route option in Timestamp Reply

constraint.value: MUST reverse the return route and use it as a Source Route option for the Timestamp Reply

rules.source_quote: If a Source-route option is received in an ICMP Echo Request, the return route MUST be reversed and used as a Source Route option for the Timestamp Reply message.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Timestamp Request with a Source Route option and verify if the Timestamp Reply uses the reversed route. Incorrect or missing reversed route violates this rule.

rules.name: Timestamp Reply processing

constraint.value: MUST be passed up to the ICMP user interface

rules.source_quote: Incoming Timestamp Reply messages MUST be passed up to the ICMP user interface.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an ICMP Timestamp Reply and verify if the AFDX End System forwards it to the ICMP user interface or drops it.

rules.name: Timestamp value format

constraint.value: milliseconds since midnight Universal Time

rules.source_quote: The preferred form for a timestamp value (the "standard value") is in units of milliseconds since midnight Universal Time.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate ICMP Timestamp messages with malformed timestamp values (e.g., negative values, values exceeding 86400000 ms) and observe network reaction.

rules.name: Address Mask source configurability

constraint.value: MUST be configurable

rules.source_quote: The choice of method to be used in a particular host MUST be configurable…

rules.name: Static address mask support
rules.source_quote: Support static configuration of address mask

rules.name: Dynamic address mask acquisition methods
rules.source_quote: (1) static configuration information… (2) obtaining the address mask(s) dynamically as a side-effect of the system initialisation process… (3) sending ICMP Address Mask Request(s) and receiving ICMP Address Mask Reply(s).

rules.name: Address Mask Request retransmission

constraint.value: MUST retransmit a small number of times if no Reply received

rules.source_quote: When method 3, it MUST retransmit this message a small number of times if it does not receive an immediate Address Mask Reply.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can simulate a scenario where no Address Mask Reply is received and observe if the AFDX End System retransmits the request a finite number of times before giving up.

rules.name: Default address mask assumption

constraint.value: SHOULD assume mask appropriate for the address class of the IP address

rules.source_quote: When method 3, until it has received an Address Mask Reply, the host SHOULD assume a mask appropriate for the address class of the IP address.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can delay or block Address Mask Replies and verify if the AFDX End System falls back to a default mask based on IP address class.

rules.name: First Address Mask Reply usage

constraint.value: MUST use the first Address Mask Reply received to set the address mask

rules.source_quote: When method 3, the first Address Mask Reply message received MUST be used to set the address mask corresponding to the particular local IP address.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send multiple Address Mask Replies with conflicting masks and observe if the AFDX End System uses only the first one received.

rules.name: Address Mask reasonableness check

constraint.value: SHOULD make some reasonableness check on any address mask it installs

rules.source_quote: A host SHOULD make some reasonableness check on any address mask it installs.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send Address Mask Replies with unreasonable masks (e.g., 0.0.0.0, 255.255.255.255, or masks not aligned with IP address class) and observe if the AFDX End System rejects them.

rules.name: Unauthorized Address Mask Reply restriction

constraint.value: MUST NOT send an Address Mask Reply unless it is an authoritative agent

rules.source_quote: A system MUST NOT send an Address Mask Reply unless it is an authoritative agent for address masks.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can configure an AFDX End System as non-authoritative and verify if it still sends Address Mask Replies, violating the rule.

rules.name: Authoritative agent configuration requirement

constraint.value: MUST be explicitly configured as an address mask agent

rules.source_quote: An authoritative agent may be a host or a gateway, but it MUST be explicitly configured as a address mask agent.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send an Address Mask Request to an AFDX End System not explicitly configured as an agent and observe if it responds with a Reply.

rules.name: Static configuration authorization flag

constraint.value: SHOULD have an additional configuration flag for authoritative agent status

rules.source_quote: With a statically configured address mask, there SHOULD be an additional configuration flag that determines whether the host is to act as an authoritative agent for this mask.

rules.name: Address Mask Reply broadcast on initialization

constraint.value: MUST broadcast an Address Mask Reply on initialization if configured as an agent

rules.source_quote: If it is configured as an agent, the host MUST broadcast an Address Mask Reply for the mask on the appropriate interface when it initializes.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can monitor an AFDX End System configured as an authoritative agent during initialization and verify if it broadcasts an Address Mask Reply.

rules.name: Address mask usage in local/remote decision

constraint.value: MUST use address mask in local/remote decision for outbound datagrams

rules.source_quote: Use address mask in local/remote decision
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate outbound IP datagrams with destination addresses and observe if the AFDX End System correctly uses the address mask to determine if the destination is local or remote.

rules.name: Static route definition requirement
rules.source_quote: AFDX is statically defined
rules.source_section: Attachment 2, IP/ICMP, UDP, and TCP Profile Provisions, RFC 1122 Paragraph 3.5
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject dynamic routing updates or attempt to modify static routes at runtime.

rules.name: Route cache maintenance requirement
rules.source_quote: The source host MUST keep a 'route cache' of mappings to next-hop gateways.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send frames without maintaining or updating a route cache.

rules.name: Route cache field inclusion requirement

value: Local IP address (for a multihomed host)

rules.source_quote: Each route cache entry needs to include the following fields: (1) Local IP address (for a multihomed host) (2) Destination IP address (3) Type(s)-of-Service (4) Next-hop gateway IP address
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could omit one or more required fields in route cache entries.

rules.name: Type of Service inclusion in route cache
rules.source_quote: The TOS SHOULD be included.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could exclude Type of Service (TOS) from route cache entries.

rules.name: Gateway failure detection requirement
rules.source_quote: The IP layer MUST be able to detect the failure of a 'next-hop' gateway that is listed in its route cache and to choose an alternate gateway.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a gateway failure without triggering failure detection or alternate gateway selection.

rules.name: Gateway usage duration constraint

constraint.value: Gateway SHOULD NOT be used indefinitely without positive indications of functionality.

rules.source_quote: A particular gateway SHOULD NOT be used indefinitely in the absence of positive indications that it is functioning.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could continuously use a gateway without any positive indication of its functionality.

rules.name: Continuous gateway pinging prohibition
rules.source_quote: hosts MUST NOT actively check the status of a first-hop gateway by simply pinging the gateway continuously.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send continuous ICMP echo requests to a gateway.

rules.name: Conditional pinging requirement

constraint.value: Pinging MUST be used only when traffic is being sent to the gateway and when there is no other positive indication to suggest that the gateway is functioning.

rules.source_quote: Pinging MUST be used only when traffic is being sent to the gateway… and when there is no other positive indication to suggest that the gateway is functioning.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send ICMP echo requests when no traffic is being sent or when positive indications of gateway functionality exist.

rules.name: Status advice from higher/lower layers requirement
rules.source_quote: the layers above and/or below the Internet layer SHOULD be able to give 'advice' on the status of route cache entries when either positive (gateway OK) or negative (gateway dead) information is available.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could ignore or suppress status advice from higher or lower layers.

rules.name: ICMP message restriction
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP 'echo request' and 'echo reply' are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could inject ICMP messages other than 'echo request' or 'echo reply'.

rules.name: Network and Host Redirect equivalence

constraint.value: Network Redirect message SHOULD be treated identically to a Host Redirect message.

rules.source_quote: a Network Redirect message SHOULD be treated identically to a Host Redirect message.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could treat Network Redirect and Host Redirect messages differently.

rules.name: Static route override flag requirement
rules.source_quote: Each such static route MAY include a flag specifying whether it may be overridden by ICMP Redirects.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could ignore or improperly set the override flag for static routes.

rules.name: Default gateway selection requirement
rules.source_quote: The IP layer MUST pick a gateway from its list of 'default' gateways.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could fail to select a default gateway when no route cache entry exists.

rules.name: Multiple default gateways support requirement
rules.source_quote: The IP layer MUST support multiple default gateways.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could restrict the IP layer to a single default gateway.

rules.name: Minimal network environment operation requirement
rules.source_quote: The host IP layer MUST operate correctly in a minimal network environment, and in particular, when there are no gateways.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a minimal network environment and verify that the IP layer fails to operate correctly.

rules.name: Default Gateway Switching on Failure

constraint.value: If the current default gateway fails, the IP layer MUST select a different default gateway.

rules.source_quote: If the failed gateway is not the current default, the IP layer can immediately switch to a default gateway. If it is the current default that failed, the IP layer MUST select a different default gateway.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a gateway failure and verify if the IP layer switches to an alternative default gateway or fails to do so.

rules.name: Manual Configuration Method Requirement
rules.source_quote: A manual method of entering this configuration data MUST be provided.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to send traffic without manual configuration or with invalid manual configuration to test enforcement.

rules.name: IP Datagram Reassembly Requirement
rules.source_quote: The IP layer MUST implement reassembly of IP datagrams.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send fragmented datagrams and verify if the IP layer reassembles them correctly or fails to do so.

rules.name: Minimum Reassembly Buffer Size
rules.source_quote: EMTU_R MUST be greater than or equal to 576, SHOULD be either configurable or indefinite, and SHOULD be greater than or equal to the MTU of the connected network(s).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send datagrams larger than 576 bytes and verify if they are reassembled or discarded.

rules.name: Transport Layer Access to MMS_R

constraint.value: There MUST be a mechanism by which the transport layer can learn MMS_R.

rules.source_quote: There MUST be a mechanism by which the transport layer can learn MMS_R.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to send datagrams exceeding MMS_R and verify if the transport layer enforces the limit.

rules.name: ICMP Time Exceeded on Reassembly Timeout

constraint.value: If reassembly timeout expires, the partially-reassembled datagram MUST be discarded and an ICMP Time Exceeded message sent to the source host (if fragment zero has been received).

rules.source_quote: If this timeout expires, the partially-reassembled datagram MUST be discarded and an ICMP Time Exceeded message sent to the source host (if fragment zero has been received).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could simulate a reassembly timeout and verify if an ICMP Time Exceeded message is sent.

rules.name: Transport Layer Access to MMS_S

constraint.value: A host MUST implement a mechanism to allow the transport layer to learn MMS_S.

rules.source_quote: A host MUST implement a mechanism to allow the transport layer to learn MMS_S.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to send datagrams exceeding MMS_S and verify if the transport layer enforces the limit.

rules.name: Local Fragmentation Optional
rules.source_quote: Optionally, the IP layer MAY implement a mechanism to fragment outgoing datagrams intentionally.

rules.name: No Local Fragmentation Enforcement

constraint.value: A host that does not implement local fragmentation MUST ensure that the transport layer or application layer does not send a datagram exceeding MMS_S in size.

rules.source_quote: A host that does not implement local fragmentation MUST ensure that the transport layer (for TCP) or the application layer (for UDP) obtains MMS_S from the IP layer and does not send a datagram exceeding MMS_S in size.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send datagrams exceeding MMS_S and verify if they are discarded or fragmented.

rules.name: Maximum Datagram Size for Off-Network Destinations
rules.source_quote: In the absence of actual knowledge of the minimum MTU along the path, the IP layer SHOULD use EMTU_S <= 576 whenever the destination address is not on a connected network.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send datagrams larger than 576 bytes to off-network destinations and verify if they are discarded or fragmented.

rules.name: Response Address Matching

constraint.value: If the datagram is sent in response to a received datagram, the source address for the response SHOULD be the specific-destination address of the request.

rules.source_quote: (1) If the datagram is sent in response to a received datagram, the source address for the response SHOULD be the specific-destination address of the request.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send a request and verify if the response uses the correct source address.

rules.name: Application Control of Source IP Address

constraint.value: An application MUST be able to explicitly specify the source address for initiating a connection or a request.

rules.source_quote: (2) An application MUST be able to explicitly specify the source address for initiating a connection or a request.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to initiate connections with invalid or mismatched source addresses and verify enforcement.

rules.name: Discard Datagram on Wrong Interface

constraint.value: A host MAY silently discard an incoming datagram whose destination address does not correspond to the physical interface through which it is received.

rules.source_quote: (A) A host MAY silently discard an incoming datagram whose destination address does not correspond to the physical interface through which it is received.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send datagrams to an interface with a mismatched destination address and verify if they are discarded.

rules.name: Restrict Outgoing Datagrams to Correct Interface

constraint.value: A host MAY restrict itself to sending (non-source-routed) IP datagrams only through the physical interface that corresponds to the IP source address of the datagrams.

rules.source_quote: (B) A host MAY restrict itself to sending (non-source-routed) IP datagrams only through the physical interface that corresponds to the IP source address of the datagrams.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could attempt to send datagrams through an interface with a mismatched source address and verify if they are discarded or sent.

rules.name: Source Routing Restriction
rules.source_quote: Source routing not allowed
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer could send datagrams with source routing options and verify if they are discarded.

rules.name: TTL Decrement Requirement for Forwarded Datagrams

constraint.value: MUST decrement TTL when forwarding a source-routed datagram

rules.source_quote: The TTL field MUST be decremented and the datagram.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send a source-routed datagram with TTL=1 and verify if the End System (ES) decrements it to 0 or forwards it without decrementing.

rules.name: ICMP Destination Unreachable Generation for Fragmentation Required
rules.source_quote: A host MUST be able to generate Destination Unreachable messages with the following codes: 4 (Fragmentation Required but DF Set) when a source-routed datagram cannot be fragmented to fit into the target network
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send a source-routed datagram with DF bit set and size exceeding the MTU to verify if the ES generates ICMP code 4.

rules.name: Non-Local Source Routing Configurable Switch
rules.source_quote: A host that supports non-local source-routing MUST have a configurable switch to disable forwarding… and this switch MUST default to disabled.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can attempt to enable non-local source routing and verify if the ES defaults to disabled or allows forwarding.

rules.name: Broadcast Address Recognition
rules.source_quote: A host MUST recognize any of these forms in the destination address of an incoming datagram: Limited Broadcast: {-1, -1}, Directed Broadcast: {<Network-number>,-1}, Subnet Directed Broadcast: {<Network-number>,<Subnet-number>,-1}, All-Subnets Directed Broadcast: {<Network-number>,-1,-1}
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send datagrams with non-standard broadcast addresses (e.g., {0, 0}) and verify if the ES recognizes them as valid broadcasts.

rules.name: Broadcast Address Format Configuration Default
rules.source_quote: A host MAY optionally have a configuration option to choose the 0 or the -1 form of broadcast address... but this option SHOULD default to the standard (-1) form.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can attempt to configure the ES to use 0-form broadcast addresses and verify if it defaults to -1 form.

rules.name: ICMP Message Restrictions
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP 'echo request' and 'echo reply' are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send ICMP messages other than echo request/reply (e.g., timestamp request) and verify if the ES drops or processes them.

rules.name: Discard invalid link-layer broadcast datagrams

constraint.value: silently_discard

rules.source_quote: A host SHOULD silently discard a datagram that is received via a link-layer broadcast (see Section 2.4) but does not specify an IP multicast or broadcast destination address.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send a frame with a link-layer broadcast address but an invalid IP destination (e.g., unicast) and verify if the frame is silently discarded by the receiving End System.

rules.name: Use Limited Broadcast address

constraint.value: SHOULD_use_limited_broadcast

rules.source_quote: Hosts SHOULD use the Limited Broadcast address to broadcast to a connected network.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a broadcast frame using a non-limited broadcast address (e.g., subnet-directed broadcast) and observe if the network prefers the limited broadcast address.

rules.name: Support local IP multicasting

constraint.value: SHOULD_support

rules.source_quote: A host SHOULD support local IP multicasting on all connected networks for which a mapping from Class D IP addresses to link-layer addresses has been specified.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send multicast frames to an End System and verify if it can join, receive, and leave multicast groups.

rules.name: Join all-hosts multicast group at startup
rules.source_quote: If IGMP is not implemented, a host SHOULD still join the 'all-hosts' group (224.0.0.1) when the IP layer is initialized and remain a member for as long as the IP layer is active.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can check if an End System joins the 224.0.0.1 multicast group at startup and remains a member.

rules.name: Pass IP options to transport layer

constraint.value: MUST_pass_all_options

rules.source_quote: The parameter opt contains all the IP options received in the datagram; these MUST also be passed to the transport layer.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send a frame with IP options and verify if the receiving End System passes all options to the transport layer.

rules.name: Include original IP header and 8+ octets in ICMP error
rules.source_quote: For an ICMP error message, the data that is passed up MUST include the original Internet header plus all the octets of the original message that are included in the ICMP message.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate an ICMP error message with fewer than 8 octets of the original message and verify if the receiving End System discards it or processes it incorrectly.

rules.name: Domain ID format in MAC address
rules.source_quote: The Domain ID should be coded with 4 bits. The 0000 and 1111 are forbidden values. Therefore, 14 Domains ID are possible.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a frame with a MAC address containing a Domain ID of 0000 or 1111 and verify if the network rejects it.

rules.name: Side ID format in MAC address
rules.source_quote: The Side ID format should be coded with 3 bits. The 000 and 111 are forbidden values.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a frame with a MAC address containing a Side ID of 000 or 111 and verify if the network rejects it.

rules.name: Location ID format in MAC address
rules.source_quote: The Location ID format should be coded with 5 bits. The 00000 and 11111 are forbidden values.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a frame with a MAC address containing a Location ID of 00000 or 11111 and verify if the network rejects it.

rules.name: Domain ID format in IP address
rules.source_quote: The Domain ID should be coded with 4 bits. The 0000 and 1111 are forbidden values.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a frame with an IP address containing a Domain ID of 0000 or 1111 and verify if the network rejects it.

rules.name: Side ID format in IP address
rules.source_quote: The Side ID format should be coded with 3 bits. The 000 and 111 are forbidden values.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a frame with an IP address containing a Side ID of 000 or 111 and verify if the network rejects it.

rules.name: Location ID format in IP address
rules.source_quote: The Location ID format should be coded with 5 bits. The 00000 and 11111 are forbidden values.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate a frame with an IP address containing a Location ID of 00000 or 11111 and verify if the network rejects it.

rules.name: Fixed-length ARINC 429 label encapsulation
rules.source_quote: Place each label in a fixed length 32-bit opaque data primitive
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with ARINC 429 labels encapsulated in non-32-bit lengths (e.g., 16-bit or 64-bit).

rules.name: Reserved field usage in single-label messages

constraint.value: Must be set to binary zeros or unused

rules.source_quote: Reserved [...] unused unused unused
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can populate reserved fields with non-zero values or random data.

rules.name: Frame Status (FS) field presence
rules.source_quote: Note that the FS represents the status of the gateway that is introducing the ARINC 429 data to the AFDX network.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can omit the FS field or corrupt its value in transmitted frames.

rules.name: Data Set (DS) field usage for multi-label messages

constraint.value: Must reflect the status of the concentrator; single DS for single-threaded devices, multiple DS for fault-tolerant concentrators

rules.source_quote: If all labels are concentrated into a single Ethernet frame by a single threaded device, a single DS should be used [...] If the concentrator device is designed in such a way that a portion of it could fail [...] more than one DS should be considered.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with mismatched DS/FS pairs or omit DS fields in multi-label messages.

rules.name: Variable-length opaque structure maximum size

constraint.value: Must be statically configured based on the maximum number of labels arriving between transmissions

rules.source_quote: The system designer must figure out what the highest or maximum number of labels is that could possibly arrive at the gateway between transmissions. From this maximum number the maximum size of the variable length opaque structure is established.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames exceeding the statically configured maximum size for variable-length opaque structures.

rules.name: Length field accuracy in variable-length messages

constraint.value: Must accurately reflect the number of bytes with valid data in the opaque structure

rules.source_quote: When it is time for transmission, the gateway will compute how many bytes of the static length have good data in them and load this number into the length field of the structure.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with mismatched length fields (e.g., length field indicating more data than present or less data than the actual payload).

rules.name: Padding of unused opaque structure bytes

constraint.value: Must be filled with binary zeros

rules.source_quote: The unused portion of the opaque field is filled with binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can populate unused bytes with non-zero values or random data.

rules.name: Transmission of entire static structure

constraint.value: Must transmit the entire statically configured structure, not just the used portion

rules.source_quote: The message is then sent, with the entire static structure, not just the used portion.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can truncate frames to only include the used portion of the opaque structure.

rules.name: AFDX_frame_encapsulation_order
rules.source_quote: A frame is the unit of transmission at Ethernet level, and consists of a MAC header followed by a packet. A packet is the unit of data passed across the interface between the IP layer and the data link layer (MAC). It includes an IP header and data. A message consists of a transport protocol header followed by application data.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames with incorrect encapsulation order, e.g., swapping IP header and UDP header or omitting the MAC header.

rules.name: UDP_datagram_fragmentation_constraint

constraint.value: UDP datagrams exceeding MTU size must be fragmented into packets.

rules.source_quote: Whenever an UDP datagram is too long to fit in a packet, it is break in an almost arbitrary number of pieces that are placed in fragments.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate oversized UDP datagrams without fragmentation or with malformed fragments (e.g., overlapping offsets).

rules.name: packet_size_limit_by_MTU

constraint.value: Maximum size of a packet is limited by the MTU of the network.

rules.source_quote: Maximum size of a packet is limited by the MTU (Max Transfer Unit) of the network.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate packets exceeding the AFDX MTU (typically 1518 bytes for standard Ethernet frames).

rules.name: AFDX_supported_protocols
rules.source_quote: Table D-1 – Services to Protocol Mapping lists protocols used in AFDX networks: IEEE-802.3, IPv4, UDP, ARP, ICMP, TFTP, BOOTP, DHCP.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can inject frames using unsupported protocols (e.g., IPv6, TCP for simple data transport) or malformed protocol headers.

rules.name: AFDX_protocol_restrictions_for_data_transport
rules.source_quote: Data Transport (simple)    X                (UDP only in Table D-1).
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate frames using TCP for simple data transport instead of UDP.

rules.name: static_message_length_for_jitter_reduction

constraint.value: Messages should use statically defined structure (fixed length) to reduce jitter.

rules.source_quote: Sending the complete, statically defined structure, helps keep the jitter in the system lower. This makes every message the same length, even though the data in the message is not all valid.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate variable-length messages or truncate static-length messages to introduce jitter.

rules.name: message_padding_for_bandwidth_allocation

constraint.value: Unused portions of a message should be padded to maintain fixed bandwidth allocation.

rules.source_quote: The bandwidth has been allocated to this data flow for the maximum size the message can be, and is not useable by any other flow. It is therefore not wasted.
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can omit padding or use non-zero padding values in messages.

rules.name: variable_length_opaque_structure_constraint
rules.source_quote: Variable Length Opaque-Static Length = 40 bytes
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate opaque structures exceeding 40 bytes or with malformed length fields.

rules.name: dynamic_message_length_constraint
rules.source_quote: Dynamic Length = 22
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate dynamic-length messages exceeding 22 bytes.
